title: When Toolbar is in text mode the bookmarks toolbar loses the "spill over" chevron icon.
description:
When Toolbar is in text mode the bookmarks toolbar loses the "spill over"
chevron icon.

Reproducible: Always

Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.2b) Gecko/20021029 Phoenix/0.4

Steps to reproduce:
1) Add many items to the Bookmark Toolbar Folder
2) Open the toolbar customization dialog
3) Change to text mode (Select Text from the show menu)

Expected: Bookmarks will fill entire bar and will indicate a dropdown list of
bookmarks that could not fit.

Actual: Drop down menu is available, however, at first inspection it would
appear that it isn't because the icon indicating the list is missing.

title: [cust] Toolbar customization dialog doesn't always fit on screen
description:
Tested with Windows 98 and Linux (GNOME2/metacity and IceWM).

Under some circumstances, the toolbar customization dialog rolls outside the 
visible desktop area. It's pretty easy to lose the "Done" button outside the 
visible area if you're not careful. If "Done" disappears, it's very hard to 
close the dialog (the workaround is to press shift-tab and then space).

Having a screen resolution like 800x600 or 640x480 makes things even more 
tricky, since the customization dialog is huge (600x400 pixels or so).

Steps to reproduce:

1) move the Phoenix window near the bottom of the screen (so that there isn't 
enough vertical space under the toolbars for the dialog to appear)
2) View/Toolbar/Customize...

or:

1) move the window to the right edge of the screen so that half of it is outside
the visible area
2) View/Toolbar/Customize...

What happens: the dialog rolls outside the screen. Very difficult to close the 
dialog (workaround: press shift-tab, then space)

Expected: should be able to edit the toolbars.

title: [cust] Window can be moved when toolbar customization dialog active; dialog doesn't move
description:
Tested with Windows 98 and Linux (GNOME2/metacity and IceWM)

Steps to reproduce:

1) View/Toolbar/Customize...
2) Move the parent window

What happens: the window moves but the dialog doesn't

Expected: window shouldn't move, or the dialog should move with it

I guess the customization dialog should block the parent window so that it can't
be moved. Normal dialogs do this, are sheets special? What does OSX do?

title: Ctrl+B should open Bookmark Manager
description:
Currently in Phoenix, Ctrl+B toggles the Bookmarks sidebar. However, Ctrl+B
opens the Bookmark Manager in Netscape 3.x, Netscape 4.x, Mozilla, and Netscape
6.x-7.x.

title: backspace should undo selecting an autocomplete entry
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.3a) Gecko/20021119 Phoenix/0.4
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.3a) Gecko/20021119 Phoenix/0.4

When auto-complete pops down a match in the URL bar and I hit TAB, it places the
next match's completion text after the cursor. If I now want to select the next
match after that, I have to hit END and then TAB again. If I want to add to the
matched URL, I have to hit END and start typing. Now if I decide I don't want
that last match, I have to Backspace thru it all and then start over. 

My suggestion is to allow matches to be selected and un-done with one use of the
TAB and Backspace key. I will try to explain this in detail below.

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1. type a partial match in the address bar and hit TAB to select the first
   suggestion.
Actual Results:  
1. the suggestion is appended to the text I entered, but the cursor is now in 
   the middle of the URL where it is not very useful.
2. If I hit Backspace, the text ahead of the cursor is deleted, leaving me with
   the text that I entered -- this is good.

Expected Results:  
Place the cursor at the end of the selected match, but remember the previous
cursor positions. A single Backspace should clear back to these positions, one
at a time, much like a typing history (analogy to the browsing history).

Ok, now to explain with an example.

Suppose I have visited 
www.foo.com
www.foo.com/bar/
www.foo.com/bar.html

1. I type 'fo' and it pops down 'www.foo.com' etc
2. I hit TAB and select 'www.foo.com' and the cursor is at the end of the text.
   I then type 'b' and it shows me the last 3 entries
3. I hit TAB and get 'www.foo.com/bar' and then start typing 'tender.html' to
   end up with 'www.foo.com/bartender.html'
4. I change my mind and hit Backspace. I BS back through 'tender.html' one char
   at a time. Once I hit the 'r' it remembers that I typed that all as one chunk
   of text and erases it as one chunk. I am now at 'www.foo.com' again.

This represents a choice: whether to optimize in favor of those who want to
auto-complete and change from the end, or in favor of easy navigation through
matches. To illustrate the first choice, suppose 'www.foo.com/bartender.html'
was actually not found, and I want to do 'www.foo.com/bartender.php' instead.
The easy way would be to autocomplete and then Backspace till 'html' was gone,
then type 'php'. My preferred behavior makes this hard. I don't think it is a
frequent problem though.

I invite discussion on this... I posted it on the forums but no replies yet.

title: Go button should not be container
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.3a) Gecko/20021227 Phoenix/0.5
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.3a) Gecko/20021227 Phoenix/0.5

This will probably get marked as Won't Fix, but I'm going to try anyways.

The XUL for the Go button is different than most of the other toolbar buttons. 
Instead of a button, it is a container.
      <toolbaritem id="go-container" align="center" class="chromeclass-location">
        <button id="go-button" class="button-toolbar"
                label="&goButton.label;"
                oncommand="addToUrlbarHistory(); BrowserLoadURL();"
                ondragover="nsDragAndDrop.dragOver(event, goButtonObserver);"
                ondragdrop="nsDragAndDrop.drop(event, goButtonObserver);"
                ondragexit="nsDragAndDrop.dragExit(event, goButtonObserver);"
                tooltiptext="&goButton.tooltip;"/> 
      </toolbaritem>

This makes theming the Go button much harder, especially when it comes to Text
Only mode.  

I suggest making it have the class toolbarbutton-1, just like Back, Forward,
Print, etc.

      <toolbarbutton id="print-button" class="toolbarbutton-1"
                      label="&printButton.label;"
                      oncommand="BrowserPrint();"
                      tooltiptext="&printButton.tooltip;"/>


Reproducible: Always

title: when unvisited link becomes visited, href attribute becomes absolute
description:
Phoenix has a feature that makes links change from the unvisited appearance to
the visited appearance when you middle-click them.  This feature has a
side-affect: the href attribute becomes absolute when a link becomes visited,
confusing my user style sheet and potentially confusing scripts that use
getAttribute("href") [as opposed to foo.href].

This bug doesn't affect links that were already visited before you load a page.
 As a result, reloading fixes the problem.

I discovered this bug shortly after adding the following rule to
userContent.css.  The rule is only supposed to match absolute links to slashdot
urls, but because of this bug, it also matches relative links to slashdot urls
that are visited while the page is open.  The rule doesn't use :link or :visited.

a[href^="http://www.slashdot.org"], a[href^="http://slashdot.org"] 
{ background: white ! important; color: #066 ! important; font-weight: bold !
important }

title: Attempting to render large numbers of listboxes completely kills WinXP desktop
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.1; en-US; rv:1.3a) Gecko/20021212
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.1; en-US; rv:1.3a) Gecko/20021212

Attempting to render a page containing a large number of listboxes (for
instance slashdot with moderator access) can cause the entire WinXP
desktop (not just Mozilla) to become unresponsive.

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1. MAKE SURE YOU HAVE SAVED EVERYTHING ON YOUR WORKSTATION!

2. Create a web page with:

    <select id="test" >
          <option value="1" selected>Testing
          </option>
    </select>

repeated 1500 or so times. The exact amount isn't critical,
but might vary depending on the system.

3. Navigate to this page using Mozilla on WinXP.


Actual Results:  
WinXP becomes unresponsive to the extent that you can't even
bring up the task manager to kill Mozilla or shutdown the system. :(


Expected Results:  
Render the page, or at least not take down the desktop.

IE 6.0 renders the page very slowly, but does not lock up.

Note that this is a security issue as it allows a denial-of-service
attack, and possible data loss on the client as it requires a hard
reboot to recover the system.

I've noticed similar problems to this using older versions of IE
on various windows platforms, but it seems to have been fixed with
the latest IE.

dblclick gets generated, nothing happens.

Open the page normaly.

title: [beos] customize toolbar window displays titlebar
description:
I have a patch prepared for the BeOS widget library, that makes nsWindow under
BeOS honor the eBorderStyle attributes of a window.  I wrote the patch, in the
hopes that the "Customize Toolbar" window would be created w/o the title bar.

However, the title bar remains.  The eBorderStyle that is passed into the
nsWindow's create method is eBorderStyle_all, so, even with my patch applied,
the window still has a titlebar. 

I've searched for where and why this is happenning, but, I'm having trouble
finding the solution.

title: Autoscroll "sticks" if a dialog appears while autoscrolling
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.3) Gecko/20030312
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.3) Gecko/20030312

When using autoscroll, if a cookie popup happens (from a middle-click opening a
URL in another tab), the autoscroll "sticks" at its speed and you have to
dismiss the cookie window before regaining control of autoscroll.

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open Slashdot or other news site with multiple links on the front page.
2. Open a link to a site you haven't been to before (using middle-click, which
(when configured properly) opens the link in a new tab and leaves you in the
original tab).
3. Immediately middle-click on whitespace, activating the autoscroll
functionality (this is installed separately, see http://autoscroll.mozdev.org/
), and move the cursor down (or up) so that the window starts scrolling.
4. When the new site attempts to set a cookie (and you've configured it to ask
you prior to setting cookies), a window pops up asking whether to allow the cookie.
5. Moving the mouse up or down has no effect on autoscroll; it continues
scrolling at the same speed in the direction it was scrolling prior to the popup
appearing.
Actual Results:  
Moving the mouse up or down has no effect on autoscroll; it continues scrolling
at the same speed in the direction it was scrolling prior to the popup appearing.

Expected Results:  
I expect the popup to temporarily disable the autoscroll, so no scrolling occurs
while focus cannot be obtained.  Or, it could just permanently disable
autoscroll and I would have to middle-click again to activate it after I dismiss
the popup.

Or, even better, the cookie popup would be "just another window" and would not
be modal (?) -- I would still be able to focus on the tab I was on, and change
to other tabs, and use Mozilla normally except there would be a separate window
with the cookie question in it.

there's a small amount of time (sometimes it's going to be up to 6 seconds) when
Fb hangs.

While fetching a single page it is hard to see but you'll notice the animated
(tab-) icon is hanging for a short time period. While the animated icon is
hanging, no mouse clicks or keyboard input is being processed (will be processed
when the page either completed rendering or will continue fetching). While Fb is
hanging you even can't switch to another open Fb window.

opened browser windows are hanging once in a while!

(03 and 04 nightlies didn't show that appearance) but the latest nightly
(2003-05-25) is doing it really bad and the delay (time while hanging) seems to
be extended (compared to mid May nightlies).

I've had to switch back to nightly 2003-05-19 which is at least useable with
that bug.

It _seems_ like pages without lots of graphics aren't causing _that much_
trouble but long pages or pages with lots of graphics appear to load with a
badly hanging browser for a few seconds.

tested using W2k SP1 US-EN, using squid 2.5-stable and wwwoffle at the LAN border.

Installed extensions: LiveHTTPHeader (disabled), NukeImage, Tabbrowser
Extensions (latest, 2003-05-20), TextLinks

Steps to Reproduce:
1. open several tabs
2. load URI

notice a hanging browser until all pages are loaded and rendered

Since (I believe) about 10 days ago, I have been getting crashes in Eudora when
launching an http link from a message.  In addition to Eudora generating an
exception error, Firebird would open with 2 windows.  One would have the
requested content, the other would be blank, and would not respond to entries in
the URL bar or to bookmark selection.
I did some playing around and seem to have fixed the problem.  The registry key
for the protocol's DDE application name
(HKCR\http\shell\open\ddeexec\application) has been changed to "Mozilla
Firebird."  I changed this back to "Phoenix" and all seems well now.  I'm
thinking the problem is with the space in the application name.
This wasn't crashing consistently before, so I am going to run for a day or so
with the "Phoenix" entry to see if it has fixed the problem (I'm sure
"MozillaFirebird" or "Mozilla_Firebird" would work just as well, but I assume it
was Phoenix and had been changed last week.)

Marking this as critical, although Firebird doesn't crash, Eudora does!

The Image Properties Window does not tell what type of image it is.  This can be
a problem when checking the images on bugzilla.

For example:
Go to http://bugzilla.mozilla.org/attachment.cgi?id=124232&action=view
Right click on the image and select properties.
Using the properties window, there is no valid way to determine what type of
image it is (aka gif, png, bmp, etc...)  You will notice the location field has
the value "http://bugzilla.mozilla.org/attachment.cgi?id=124232&action=view"

Thus, for cases like this, either an "Image Type:" or a "Type:" or a "File Type"
field would be useful to indicate what type of image it is.

----------------------
Here's one suggested layout of where to place the new field:

Location:
Width:
Height:
Size of File:
File Type:
Alternatate text:

A suggested formatting of the "File Type" value could be as follows (note it is
similar to the Size of File field).

EXTENSION (Description)
GIF (Graphics Interlaced Format)
PNG (Portable Network Graphics)
BMP (Bitmap)
JPG,JPEG (Joint Photographic ? Group?)

title: Use backspace key for back function in Linux
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686) Gecko/20030430 Galeon/1.3.4 Debian/1.3.4.20030509-1
Build Identifier: 

The most common actions I take in my browser are:

* search with google
* go to location bar, type in an address or nickname
* paste in an address by middle-clicking on the window
* click on a link
* go back (especially when doing google searches)
* reload (especially for nicknamed or bookmarked pages)
* copy address and paste into another app

All of these should have keyboard shortcuts. And they do. 

But back and reload are very simple actions that should have single key shortcuts. 

Currently on Unix the shortcuts are awkward to find with the fingers: Alt-Left
and Ctrl-R. 

They should be the same as on Windows: Backspace and F5. If that's not possible,
other keys should be found so that only a single, easy-to-find-with-the-fingers,
key needs to be pressed for these extremely common actions.

Thanks for your work on free software.

title: Form's onSubmit event it is not handled correctly by the browser engine
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.4b) Gecko/20030516 Mozilla Firebird/0.6
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.4b) Gecko/20030516 Mozilla Firebird/0.6

This URL is using a JavaScript validation based on form's onSubmit event. If the
JavaScript function called on that event returns false, the page should NOT be
submitted, but the Mozilla browser does! To test behaviour, use a IE based
browser, and press the submit button of the page ("Check it!" button). Do the
same with Mozilla. And this is not happening only with this page, I did my own
tests and this behaviour is the same.

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1.Use IE based browser and navigate to
http://www.peterbailey.net/fValidate/site.php?page=demo
2.Press the Check it! button and notice behaviour 
3.Use Mozilla and navigate to the same url
4.Press the Check it! button and notice the bad behaviour 

Actual Results:  
Mozilla browser will submit the page, even the onSubmit="return
validateForm(this,1,1,1,0);" function returns a FALSE!


Expected Results:  
of course, it should handle the "false" value returned by the JavaScript
validateForm function.

Imagine that you are on a page that has REQUIRED fields checked/enforced by
JavaScript using onSubmit event of the form! The user will press the "Save"
button and if there's bad development (not checking the values again on the
server side) you might end up with BIG errors (for instance this is the page
where a customer MUST enter his personal information for an on-line purchase).
I think it's pretty ugly.

title: Middle-click (or control click) on selected text to invoke Web Search (in a tab)
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030706 Mozilla Firebird/0.6 StumbleUpon/1.66
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030706 Mozilla Firebird/0.6 StumbleUpon/1.66

Context: I love being able to middle-click on a link to open it in a new tab. I
also love Web Search.

This, I think, leads naturally to my suggested enhancement: middle-click (or
control click) on /selected text/ (rather than a link) invokes the Web Search
feature (as currently found in the context menu).

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Select some text.
2. Middle-click (or control click) over the selection.

Actual Results:  
Autoscroll mode is toggled.

Expected Results:  
Web Search is invoked, with the results appearing in either a new tab or new
window depending on preference settings, and that tab/window being loaded in the
background, or immediately gaining focus, again depending on preference settings.

It's very possible, probable even, that this suggested feature could (and if so,
should) be implemented via an extension (if it's going to get implemented at all
of course). I'm assuming one is still supposed to file bugs here, regardless.]

Possible refinement #1: Put the results in a new tab (rather than a new Window,
as Web Search does at the moment). This should probably depend on the existing
related pref settings to do with opening stuff in tabs/windows. See also bug
#133117.

Possible refinement #2: Load the results in the background, keeping focus in the
clicked window rather than immediately switching focus to the new tab/window.
This should possibly depend on the existing related pref settings to do with
loading stuff in tabs in the background.

Wrinkle #1: What if selected text includes a link and one middle-clicks on the
selected link? I think Web Search should take precedence for a bunch of reasons.
I think this is obvious. I can explain if need be.

Wrinkle #2: At the moment, middle-click also toggles autoscroll mode. I'm
assuming that someone will fix this so that middle-clicking over a link has no
effect on autoscroll mode. If this feature here is implemented, the same should
apply if middle-clicking over selected text.

I think this feature might also nicely cover bug #10080; one could select the
link, middle/control click, and then google would dutifully ask "Did you mean:
http://foo.bar.baz/...".

title: Small Icons checkbox moves away from cursor when clicked - Toolbars Customize interface
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030721 Mozilla Firebird/0.6
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030721 Mozilla Firebird/0.6

Clicking the "Use Small Icons" checkbox causes the Toolbars to be resized, which
in turn causes the Customize pane to move (which is 'attached' to the toolbars).
This causes the checkbox that has just been clicked to jump out from under the
cursor.
This is a little annoying, becuase you can't sit there and toggle between the
two states quickly. In order to compare the two states you must reposition the
cursor for each click/change.
(Similar behaviour occurs with the drop down list box (DDLB) when switching
between "Icons", "Icons and Text" and "Text" modes. However, this is not as big
an issue because DDLBs do not lend themselves to fast toggling, and hence a user
would not expect to be able to do this)

Further thoughts....
Given the nature of the implementation of the Customize pane, I cannot envisage
a quick fix - it seems to be an inherent result of having the pane attached to
the toolbars. Detaching the pane is possible, or perhaps just stretching the
"connective tissue" at the top (so to speak) whenever a toolbar resize occurs.
Another possibility (albeit ultra nasty and messy and likely to cause more
problems than it solves) is to move the checkbox within the pane itself ...
urrghh - no no, forget it.

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Run MozillaFirebird.exe
2. Click View > Toolbars > Customize ...
3. If necessary, switch to "Icon" or "Icon and Text" view
4. Click the checkbox for "Use Small Icons" to change its state (change to on or
off - it doesn't matter)

Actual Results:  
The toolbars are resized.
The Customize pane moves up or down accordingly, taking the "Use Small Icons"
checkbox with it, away from the cursor

Expected Results:  
It would be nice if the checkbox for "Use Small Icons" did not jump away from
the cursor. See the "Description" for some musings

title: When dragging links, the Close Tab icon should change to a New Tab icon
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.1; en-US; rv:1.4b) Gecko/20030516 Mozilla Firebird/0.6
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.1; en-US; rv:1.4b) Gecko/20030516 Mozilla Firebird/0.6

Firebird's Close Tab widget also serves as a drop target for links. This is
especially important when several tabs are open and no space is left for the
drop target (I will soon attach a screenshot that shows this problem).

Rational:
1. Dropping links on the tab bar (to open new tabs) is one of four supported
ways to open a link in a new tab.
2. During this drag&drop operation, the *only* functionality of the Close Tab
widget is to provide a drop target for new tabs. It can't be used for closing
tabs while a link is being dragged.
3. Using a Close Tab icon |X| as a drop target is counter-intuitive. The icon
hints for closing an object, not for spawning one.

See the OS X Trash as a good example of a widget that changes its icon to
reflect a different action during a drag. When the user drags a folder or a
file, it looks (and acts) as a Trash bin; when the user drags a mounted disk/CD,
it looks (and acts) as an eject button.

Prog.

Reproducible: Always

title: Browser Crashes in Password Manager
description:
I visit a particular site, and as the password manager attempts to complete my
login information the browser crashes in:

nsPasswordManager::OnStateChange

at:       passField->SetValue(buffer);

('passField' is null...) Adding a null check for passField caused it to crash a
couple of lines further up ('nameField' is null...)

It seems that it is possible to get into a state where you exit the loop over
all the SignonDataEntries and 'firstMatch' is NON-NULL and yet 'nameField' and
'passField' are null. 

Here's why I think this is happening - 

For this site my password file has THREE entries ... not exactly sure why,
possibly related to the old password manager. The loop in OnStateChange iterates
through each entry... the first entry is invalid - the username field is
identified by a 'name' attribute that does not exist in the document, so
userField is null the loop continues to the next iteration. The next entry has
valid username and password form names and so firstMatch is set to the entry,
and the loop continues. 

The third time through, the final SignonDataEntry contains bad data, i.e.
strings that don't match the name attribute of any form element in the current
form. As such, 'userField' is null and the loop continues, but since I only have
three entries for this site, it stops iterating at this point and continues past
the loop. 

Note now that 'firstMatch' was set when we found the correct password entry
during the SECOND iteration, but that 'nameField' was set to null during the
THIRD iteration when we failed to find a form element for the name field
specified in that entry. Since 'firstMatch' is non-null, we enter the if { }
block after the loop and subsequently crash when we try to dereference the null
pointer that is nameField. 

My first reaction was to put a null check for nameField and passField in the if
block condition, but I realized this would only fix the crash, and would result
in the fields not being autocompleted because of the third, bad data entry
interfering with the second, good one. 

So I'm proposing this fix...

Change this pattern:

form->ResolveName(e->userField, getter_AddRefs(foundNode));
userField = do_QueryInterface(foundNode);
if (!userField)
  continue;

to this one:

form->ResolveName(e->userField, getter_AddRefs(foundNode));
if (foundNode)
  userField = do_QueryInterface(foundNode);
else
  continue;

where the userField variable is only updated if this data entry is legitimate. 

A patch is attached.

title: "Advanced" panel in prefs is not good UI
description:
Spin-off from bug 187989 as requested.

Firebird recently acquired an "Advanced" panel. This is bad UI for the
following reasons :

o it does not label the contents semantically (user does not know what's
in there, and will end up searching it)
o definitions of what "Advanced" means vary between users. Why is enabling
auto-scrolling advanced ? Why am I an "advanced" user if I want to load tabs
in the background ?
o it humiliates the user ("you're too stupid to see what's in here"). This
sounds like a frivolous point, but it is not.
o Advanced panels historically tend to encourage "dump any and all prefs there
without regards to design"

A solution would require a re-working of the current categories in all
likelihood, and some thought about future expansion. As the current plans
seem to be to add lots and lots more prefs by default, there's little point
attempting a redesign currently (but of course, this does not invalidate
the bug itself)

title: extreme sluggishness of bookmarks editor vs Moz 1.4
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 5.5; Windows NT 5.0)
Build Identifier: Mozilla Firebird 0.6.1

I have a pretty big bookmarks file (660 kB), which I keep on a network
drive to ensure that it gets backed up nightly. With Moz thru 1.4
final, editing this file was not problematic, despite the relative
slowness of the network connection.

I just switched to Firebird 0.6.1, and am mostly happy. But, under
Firebird, not only is there a much greater delay between C-b and the
appearance of the bookmarks tree than there is in Moz 1.4, but
individual operations (e.g. create a new folder, move bookmarks
between folders) take _much_ longer than under Moz 1.4.

This is aggravated by the apparent removal of the ability to {select,
drag'n'drop} more than one bookmark at a time: S-click and C-click
both open the selected bookmark, so there appears to be no way to,
e.g., select several bookmarks and move them all to a folder. Instead,
one must move one at a time, and each operation is _very_ slow.

It's so bad that I'm using IE to post this bug, rather than wait for
Firebird to finish editing!


Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
0.Have large bookmarks file on network drive.
1.C-b.
2.Create a folder.
3.Drag a bookmark into the folder.

Actual Results:  
Minutes pass after steps 1, 2, and 3.

Expected Results:  
Promptly completed, as in Moz 1.4.

title: Offline: should offer to clear session
description:
We currently do not have any UI or mechanism for clearing session cookies,
outside of restarting the browser application session. (This should work within
quicklaunch, but is limited by non-browsing windows hanging open, like chatzilla
or IM in N6/7).

I've been saying for a long time that we need to make Offline-Online be more
robust, taking many useful lessons from the way the MailNews features are coded
around it.

I've linked this bug up to several other related bugs.

For example, there should be a preference for cookies  that says:

When going offline -> "delete session cookies" [yes] [no] [ask me]

Also, if there were network profiles that were zone based, you could have a UI
like this:

<Work VPN>

When leaving this network:

[ ] release all session cookies for: (all|zone1|zone2) 

(where zone1 or zone2 would be defined as things like "all intranet servers" or
"my favorite ecomerce sites".

title: Basic Auth details are not sent pre-emptively
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030730 Mozilla Firebird/0.6.1
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030730 Mozilla Firebird/0.6.1

RFC2617 says "A client MAY preemptively send the corresponding Authorization
header with requests for resources in that space without receipt of another
challenge from the server."

All versions of IE, Netscape, Opera, and Mozilla *do* choose to preemprively
send Auth headers.  Firebird 0.6.1 does not; instead, it only ever sends auth
headers in response to 401 challenges.

The behaviour causes broken behaviour in the Zope CMF, and probably other web
applications which assume pre-emptive auth headers.  You could correctly argue
that these applications are broken in their assumptions, but (a) why change from
the default behaviour in all other browsers, and (b) always waiting for a
challenge is wasteful and will increase latency.

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1. visit a site which uses basic auth
2. log the HTTP headers
3. note that in Firebird, any request to that address / realm will always need
two requests, because credentials are not sent pre-emptively.

Actual Results:  
Digest of HTTP Headers:

> GET /Firebird.html
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized

> GET /Firebird.html
> Authorization: Basic AWRtaWrtZmJHLHltdxJXZ1I=

< HTTP/1.1 200 OK

Expected Results:  
> GET /Firebird.html
> Authorization: Basic AWRtaWrtZmJHLHltdxJXZ1I=

< HTTP/1.1 200 OK

title: blank entries in satchel drop-down
description:
OK, this may be hard to follow (especially because I'm super excited to have
found a 100% reproducible technique for this long-standing bug), but I'll try my
best.

Symptoms: satchel drop-down selection list SHOULD should N entries, and has
enough room for N entries, but the spot where the Nth should be is blank.

Reproducing: build a form memory with the following entries:
  foo
  foo blah
  foo testing
  foo reproduce

Now reload the page.

1) Type 'f'. See all four entries.
2) Type 'oo'. "foo" disappears. (see bug 217640 which I recently filed)
3) Type space. All three entries still shown, as expected.
NOTE: at this point, backspacing back to "fo" would behave properly. The four
      entries would be shown.
4) Now type a character that doesn't match anything. 'x'.
5) All matches disappear. This is correct.
6) Backspace. The three entries reappear. This is correct.
7) Backspace twice more, to "foo", then to "fo". Now you SHOULD again
have four entries. And there is space for four. But only three are shown. If you
arrow down to the fourth, the text field changes to it properly, so perhaps
there's some off-by-one in the code that shows matches, but not in the code
which selects an entry for the text field.

I believe there may be other circumstances which cause this pseudo-blank satchel
entry, but I'm hoping these instructions for reproduction can help track down
the root cause.

I think with a little more tweaking, satchel can become a usability win for FB
over IE. I'm eager to see these seemingly minor problems eliminated.

a definition for hover for contextual styles (div#main p:hover) and at the
alternate stylesheet it doesn't define it again, this hover will remain at the
alternate stylesheet. Then the new stylesheet must redefine it (div#main

that it changes its background color

8. Move the cursor over the paragraph inside div#main and see that it continues
 changing its background color.

Actual Results:  
It continues changing its background color even that style2.css don't define a
hover class.

Expected Results:  
I think that it should clear all style definitions and read only from the
alternate style without the need to redefine them, but I don't know what are the
standards to this operation, or, if I do need to redefine all hover that I
defined at the main style.

In a <table>, for instance:
<td background="http://us.a1.yimg.com/us.yimg.com/a/my_ad_here.gif">

The image will still be blocked if the user had selected "Block images from this
server" previously, but when right-clicking on this ad, the "Block images from
this server" menu item does not appear!

Similarly, if a browser plugin is installed that enhances image blocking, such
as AdBlock for Firebird, it will not be inserted into the right-click menu.  The

(block image, save image, and so on) are not shown!

See above.

Mozilla should have treated the background image as any other image, with full
context menu items (saving, blocking, and so on).

started.

if you use multiple profiles but use 1 bookmark file,
ex  ~/.phoenix/default/xxxxxxx.slt  uses bookmark file ~/.phoenix/bookmark.html

should save to the bookmark.html file when a bookmark is added not when exiting. 

even cooler would be if the bookmarks access button would actively check the

title: Typing with dead keys does not work correctly in GTK2 builds
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.5b) Gecko/20030916 Firebird/0.6.1+
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.5b) Gecko/20030916 Firebird/0.6.1+

Firebird built with GTK2 doesn't seem to pay any attention to the definitions of
what dead keys (e.g. "dead_circumflex") set in 
/usr/X11R6/lib/X11/locale/en_US.UTF-8/Compose (in RedHat 9). Instead it seems to
use some default definitions. Thus "dead_circumflex" + a does produce "â", but
"dead_circumflex" + c does not produce "ĉ" (c with circumflex), although that is
what is defined in "Compose", and although that works in all other (Unicode
capable) programs, and in all non-GTK2 builds of Firebird and Mozilla.
"dead_circumflex" + u produces "û" although I've redefined it to produce "ŭ" (u
with breve) in "Compose" (which works in all other programs, e.g. KDE programs,
and in non-GTK2 builds of Firebird and Mozilla). Other custom keyboard
definitions done with "Xmodmap" do work, e.g. the "dead_circumflex" is on the
key where I put it, but it does not do the things I've defined in "Compose".

I can type the above mentioned special characters if I define them with e.g.
AltGr in my Xmodmap file. Only when they're defined with dead key combinations,
the problem occurs.

This is most probably a problem with GTK2 itself, since I've seen the exact same
problem in a GTK2 build of the text editor Vim. But I thought it needed to be
reported for Firebird as well. Actually as long as this bug is in GTK2 (if there
is where it is) GKT2 builds of Firebird are defective.

Most probably the same bug shows up in GTK2 builds of Mozilla (if there are any
such builds).


Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Make some custom redifinitions of dead keys in "Compose" (make sure they work
in e.g. a Unicode aware console.
2. Try to type the customs characters (e.g. in the URL field) in a GTK2 build of
Firebird


Actual Results:  
The custom definitions where ignored.

Expected Results:  
It should have used my custom definitions just like all other programs do, and
just like non-GKT2 builds of Firebird do.

title: After entering a city and state under "find a home", on the next page website never thinks that you've entered a location
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.1; en-US; rv:1.5b) Gecko/20030917 Firebird/0.6.1+
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.1; en-US; rv:1.5b) Gecko/20030917 Firebird/0.6.1+

http://www.realtor.com will never allow you to continue past the second page
when using the "find a home" feature.  A message pops-up indicating that you
need to select one or more areas.  You can select as many as you like, but you
will always get the message.

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Go to http://www.realtor.com
2. Enter a city and state (it doesn't matter which city/state)
3. Click Go
4. On the next page you can select additional cities or just click "Show properties"
Actual Results:  
After clicking "Show properties", a message pops up asking you to select one or
more area to search, regardless of how many areas you've selected.

Expected Results:  
You should continue on to the next page, which lists the homes found in the
areas that you've selected.

This works fine in internet explorer.

title: Was "Close Button fails after upgrade" (now everything locks)
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.5b) Gecko/20030917 Firebird/0.6.1+
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.5b) Gecko/20030917 Firebird/0.6.1+

It seems that everytime I grab a new "nightly build" of Firebird, after
installing and using my "original" .phoenix folder the Close Button fails to work.. 
Using "Close" from the Menu, File > Close or Quit works fine..

The fix for me is to "hide" my original .phoenix folder and work with the new
one the Firebird makes when first run and the problem is fixed.. and then just
reinstall all my extensions/Themes again..

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1.Install a new FireBird build
2.Use my original .phoenix folder
3.Close button does not work

Actual Results:  
After install using my "normal" .phoenix folder the "Close Button" does not
work, Close (Ctrl W) or Quit from the File Menu works ok..


Expected Results:  
After a fresh install and using my "original" .phoenix folder the Close widget
should work...

title: Ability to add domains to the "Pop-up Allow" list without having to go into firebird options.
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030921 Mozilla Firebird/0.6.1
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030921 Mozilla Firebird/0.6.1

It would be a very handy feature to be able to add domains to the Pop-up Allow
list from a menu in the menu bar.  There are quite a few sites I go to that
require pop-ups for log-in's or processing creditcard purchases online, or other
reasons.  As it stands, I have to go into Tools --> Options --> Web Features -->
Click Add --> and type or paste the domain name in, to allow popups from these
sites.  

It's really not that big of a deal, but it would be a very nice option to have.

title: Firebird "exit" on certain for submissions
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030728 Mozilla Firebird/0.6.1
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030728 Mozilla Firebird/0.6.1

Certain search field entry data on said website "exits" Firebird. No sign of a
crash. Acts like a normal exit.

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Go to www.icmaster.com
2. Enter electronic part number 2sc5802 in the search field on left column.
3. Firebird "exits"
4. Many other part numbers, like "LM324" will not "exit" Firebird.

Actual Results:  
Firebird exits with the odd part number and not others.

Mousewheel stops working if page loads while browser minimised
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-GB; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030728 Mozilla Firebird/0.6.1
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-GB; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030728 Mozilla Firebird/0.6.1

I have found that if a page loads while Firebird is minimised, the mousewheel
will no longer function until the page has been reloaded.  This is true for all
pages.  I have found this under both 2000 (SP3, SP4) and XP (SP1).  I was using
the standard MS mouse driver.

Reproducible: Sometimes

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Click link
2. Minimise browser during loading period
3. Try using mousewheel
4. Reload page to fix
Actual Results:  
Problem didn't occur... however, this has happened to be a lot and always when I
minimised the browser.  Unsure as to whether this is specific to page type,
state of page load, etc.  Especially common on forums of the ubb style.

Expected Results:  
Page should load, mousewheel should work.

Browser is running default theme.
Happens with and without extensions running.

title: plugins window should be resizable and retain its size
description:
The plugins window in Tools-Options-Downloads-PlugIns should be resizable like
the Password Manager, the Cookies windows and the Image Manager. I'd like to see
all plugins at once. If it becomes resizable, it should retain its size.

title: Firebird handles a common malformed Content-Type HTTP header gracelessly
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030922 Mozilla Firebird/0.6.1
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.5a) Gecko/20030922 Mozilla Firebird/0.6.1

On several web pages (including the one referenced in URL), my attempt to open
the page normally fails.  Instead, it gives the "Opening" dialog box, with the
message "The file <whatever> is of type iso-8859-1 (HyperText Markup Language),
and Mozilla Firebird does not know how to handle this file type.  This file is
located at: ... What should Mozilla Firebird do with this file?".  Going to the
same page with Mozilla displays the page normally.

Digging deeper, all the pages I get this message on include an HTTP header of
"Content-Type: text/html; charset=Shift_JIS,ISO-8859-1".  According to my
reading of RFC2616 (14.17, 3.7, 3.6, 2.2) this line is invalid HTTP (it wants a
token or a quoted string after the =, and the comma in "Shift_JIS,ISO-8859-1"
makes it neither).  The principle error is clearly on the side of the website,
not on Firebird's end.

However, even though it is a misformed header, it appears to be parsing it as if
it said "Content-Type: ISO-8859-1".  My guess is it's treating the comma as a
separator (as per RFC2616), and reading it as a list of two media types,
"text/html; charset=Shift_JIS" and "ISO-8859-1".  Since there can be only one
Content-Type for a page, it takes the last one.

This strikes me as graceless, and not following the Principle of Least Surprise.    
Mozilla properly displays these sites as text/html.  Could the algorithm that
Firebird uses to parse the HTTP headers be changed to more closely match
Mozilla's, or otherwise tweaked to use the first media type rather than the last
for Content-Type?

Thank you very much for your time, attention, and a great browser!

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1.Go to (via bookmark, address box, link, whatever) any page with the
appropriate http header

Actual Results:  
It gives the "Opening" dialog box, with the message "The file <whatever> is of
type iso-8859-1 (HyperText Markup Language), and Mozilla Firebird does not know
how to handle this file type.  This file is located at: ... What should Mozilla
Firebird do with this file?".

Expected Results:  
Rendered the page as type text/html

title: Bookmarks manager - problem interpreting ampersands in imported bookmarks
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.1; en-US; rv:1.6a) Gecko/20030926 Firebird/0.7+
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.1; en-US; rv:1.6a) Gecko/20030926 Firebird/0.7+

Whenever I delete my Firebird main and profile folders and reinstall Firebird, I
have to import my old bookmarks to be able to access them.  When this happens,
it appears Firebird wants to edit my bookmarks.html file and replace all & that
are not followed by character entity codes with & to make the code more
valid.  For example this:
http://forums.devshed.com/forumdisplay.php?s=&forumid=5

would be converted to this:
http://forums.devshed.com/forumdisplay.php?s=&forumid=5

The problem comes when I try to open these bookmarks.  For some reason the &
is not parsed out of the URL into a & and the second URL of above is sent
through.  This often breaks the CGI scripts the query string is sent to.

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1.  On a clean install, import a bookmarks.html file with a bookmark whose URL
contains an ampersand.
2.  Open the bookmark.

Actual Results:  
The location bar shows the original URL with all "&" replaced by "&".

Expected Results:  
The location bar should show the original unadulterated URL with all "&" still
intact.

It's worth noting this is only a problem with bookmarks and not hyperlinks in
downloaded files.

title: New window uses small icons even though original window has large icons
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Win98; en-US; rv:1.5b) Gecko/20030904 Firebird/0.6.1+
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Win98; en-US; rv:1.5b) Gecko/20030904 Firebird/0.6.1+

New window uses small icons even though original window has large icons:

If iconsize="small" is in localstore, and then you switch to large icons, new
windows you launch will still have small icons.  This condition continues until
you close a window that has large icons, after which new windows will have large
icons.

I fixed this issue as a part of my patch for bug 173444.  However, that
particular part of the patch was not checked in, so this is the spinoff bug. 
The issue, I believe, was first mentioned in bug 171731 comment 1 and bug 171731
comment 2.


Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
0. Create / Use new profile.
1. Observe localstore.rdf has no toolbar info in it.
2. View -> Toolbars -> Customize...
3. Uncheck "Use Small Icons" checkbox.
4. Press "Done" button.
5. Observe localstore.rdf has iconsize="" for browser.xul#toolbar-menubar,
#navigator-toolbox, #PersonalToolbar, and #nav-bar
6. View -> Toolbars -> Customize...
7. Check "Use Small Icons" checkbox.
8. Press "Done" button.
9. Observe localstore.rdf has iconsize="small" for the aforementioned elements.
10. View -> Toolbars -> Customize...
11. Uncheck "Use Small Icons" checkbox.
12. Press "Done" button.
13. Observe localstore.rdf has no toolbar iconsize info in it.

So, even though the toolbar icons are currently large (or rather, 'not small'),
there is no indication in localstore.rdf that this is their state.

14. File -> New Window

Actual Results:  
A new window appears with small icons.  This is because there is no information
currently in localstore.rdf, and the default for the toolbox and toolbars in
browser.xul is iconsize="small".


Expected Results:  
A new window appears with large icons (the same size that the first window has).


The problem happens because the setAttribute function in customizeToolbar.js
will _remove_ the attribute if null is passed as the value, and null is used to
represent a switch to "large" icons in updateIconSize(aUseSmallIcons):

  var val = aUseSmallIcons ? "small" : null;
  setAttribute(gToolbox, "iconsize", val);

The issue is worked around if we s/null/"large"/ above, so that the custom
setAttribute() does not remove the attribute.

Alternately (though I have not yet tested this), we could use the DOM's
setAttribute instead of the custom function:  gToolbox.setAttribute("iconsize",
val); etc...

I'll attach a patch later.

David

title: [altss] Style sheet selector does not display "No Theme" for pages without a base stylesheet (but shows Basic Theme)
description:
For pages having alternate stylesheets but where there is no base stylesheet
(eg, a lack of a stylesheet without a title attribute), the style sheet selector
does not display 'No Theme' but instead only displays 'Basic Theme' along with
the titles of the other themes on that page. This is incorrect - such pages do
not have a base or basic theme/style to speak of. Moreover, selecting 'Basic
Theme' does what 'No Theme' usually does - completely strips all styling from
the page, whereas on pages with both 'No Theme' and 'Basic Theme' the latter
just strips the styling of the alternate stylesheets but not that of the
untitled base theme.

At present, Asa's blog is an example of such a page. I'm also going to attach a
pair of test cases.

title: Using "|" (pipe) as URI separator breaks some links/home pages; causes multiple tabs to open
description:
Discovered initially by someone trying to check mail from yahoo messenger, but
the login URL uses two | characters, so if Firebird is not open, it breaks this
into three tabs.  Since | is a valid character in URLs, we can't exactly blame
yahoo here.

Either we need to send multiple homepage URLs to multiple prefs,  with an
integer pref for how many are currently set (since if we go from 4 to 3, we
couldn't delete browser.homepage.URL.4, just limit the loop to the number of
active homepages) or we need to come up with a different separator that's not a
valid URI character and can still be passed to Firebird on startup, however I'm
not sure if we need to support multiple pages from external apps/command line

The workaround is to open Firebird before checking mail.

Note to people cced on the bug, bug 217370 has been obsoleted in favour of a
clean bug.

it's target to _blank a window will open and jus sit there doing nothing.

actual handler for the opened url. Appart from edonkey urls (ed2k://) and mail
urls (mailto:) etc there are a lot of protocols that get registed in windows
which Firebird itself cannot handle (mms: rtsp: to name another few).

url on to the shell.

	class path is a system file that captures the shared build path information.

	change there is a potentional for conflicting changes to the class path.

	outgoing system files (same as the navigator and packages view provide).

[JFace] EC: TreeViewer refresh flickers (1GIV6K3)
description:
From EC post: "TreeViewer doUpdateItem() optimization" by DS on Aug 19, 2001:

I am using a TreeViewer to build my Outline View Trees and I noticed that
if I call refresh() it makes the tree flicker.  
There are some times when I need to call refresh() because I have cases
where I do multiple updates to my tree model and it is just easier to call
refresh()then figure out what has changed (besides refresh() is recursive,
which is exactly what I would have to do to see what has been modified).

In either case I will try to bore you with the details but after I call
refresh() the entire tree flickers and I think it is because
internalRefresh(Widget,Object,boolean) calls
updateItem((Item)widget,element) which calls ... which calls
doUpdateItem(Item item, Object element) for every node.  This is ok but it
calls this method even if Item has not changed.

I tried some things and it seems like the following fixed my problem


There is one more check but why do the update if the Text or the Image has
not changed?  I am assuming as soon as I call item.setText(text) the tree
knows that it has to update this.

Does anyone see any side effects with this?

---
NOTES:

NE (8/22/01 10:33:04 AM)
Dave,

Thanks for the suggestion.  We actually had similar checks in TableViewer at
one point, but took them out because getting the text and image were a
noticeable performance hit.  In most of our cases, the flicker wasn't too
bad.  It may be worse for trees though.
It may be possible to push this comparison down into SWT, and minimize the
performance hit.  I'll discuss it with the SWT team.

The refresh updates all items because that's how refresh is spec'ed.  The
labels may have changed, even if the same elements are there.
It would be nice to have a flag indicating whether labels should be updated
for existing elements.
We are considering adding this for 2.0.

title: [resources] API: Setting file time stamp
description:
VCM needs a Core-supported way of getting / setting the
file's modification stamp in order to be compatible with
the CVS command-line client's mechanism for determining
if files are dirty (have been changed since last checkout).

Current workaround is to obtain an instance of a java.io.File
and use lastModified() / setLastModified().  In the case of
setLastModified() we follow-up the request with a refreshLocal
to avoid resource out of sync errors.

title: Usability: Must select correct element to launch (1GEMBEL)
description:
jkca (5/31/2001 8:22:55 PM)
	jre-sdk 116

This is an issue with the algorithm for determining which element to launch.

To Duplicate:
1. Create Java Project
2. Create java file, Main.java, with a main method
3. Create java file, Other.java, without a main method
4. Select Other.java and hit run.
5. Click next in the launch wizard.
6. Nothing shows up in the list to run (but Main is right there!).

Proposed algorithm:

If the leaf of a resource tree cannot be launched, check it's parent 
node to see if it can be launched.  If you only check the parent, and 
not up the entire tree, you can be fast and correct 98% of the time. 

Perhaps the correct way to change this is for the java launcher to
do the parent check.  This way you don't have to change the debug core
right now, but the behaviour is much more user friendly.

DW (6/1/01 7:29:12 AM)
	Yes. Suggest the fix is in the java launcher - i.e. if there are no targets found
	then go back up the hierarchy looking for a target - or jump right to the project
	to look for more targets.

title: Outliner works strange on duplicate methods (1GF7GIF)
description:
Steps to reproduce :
		1) Create a class (test)
		2) type in the following:    public void one() {}
		3) Below that method type the following:   public void two() {}
		4) Below that method type the following:   public void one() {}
		5) Save the class. (There should be two errors)
		6) Delete the top method.

		When you select the "one" method in outliner, there are no selection in editor.

See : 1GE2Z8G: ITPJUI:ALL - Java Reconciler works strange on duplicate methods

NOTES:

OT (25/09/2001 5:35:27 PM)
	The problem seems to come from the occurrence count for the second method one(). The occurrence count is incremented to handle duplicate, but it is never decremented when one of the
	duplicates is removed. Then the select in the outliner view cannot retrieve the right method, because it is looking for a second method one(). Right now I have no idea where to add an
	update to adjust the occurrence count of the remaining duplicates.

OT(26/09/2001 11:17:40 AM)
	The problem results from an inconsistency in the handles after the deletion. Ideally the Java model should get rid of all the handles related to the compilation unit after the deletion of a 
	sourceRefElement, because all the occurrence counts are potentially inconsistent. But these handles seem to be persisted by the outliner. So for now there is no other solution than
	to refresh completely the outliner tree after an operation on the working copy (deletion, addition, etc.), which would make it very ugly.

OT(27/09/2001 12:02:55 PM)
	A java element is created with an occurrence count. This occurrence count is used to handle duplicates inside the Java Model. The problem that this PR points to is that removing
	an element should update the occurrence count of all duplicates of this element. This is not done through the Delete operation. Then all the handles persisted by the outline are 
	out of sync with the current content of the working copy and this leads to error in the localization of existing methods. I don't see an easy way to handle this case. Refreshing the UI
	would be one. Of course this doesn't solve the problem we have to maintain the consistency of existing handles.

title: BuildAll with curcular dependencies fails but builds with JAVAC
description:
Customers have been reporting problems trying to build large applications 
(i.e.  more than 35 projects).
Although there are several scenarios that this problems occurs, the simpliest 
way to think of this is 
then a customer starts with a new workspace, loads the source of the large 
application and selects Rebuild All.
The result is a few thousand errors in the task list.  The same source can be 
built using JAVAC (i.e builds
with out any errors).

The difference in the build results between using JAVAC and Eclipse appears to 
related to circular dependencies.
The reasons for having circular dependencies in these large applications varies 
with each customer.  From the
customer's point of view they have many developers using this structure and 
their nightly builds (using JAVAC)
build without any errors.  Thus they expect the IDE to be able to build the 
same code without errors.  In addition
waiting for V2 of Eclipse is not a alternative for these customers.  Also 
building individual projects is also not
alternaitve since it can take a long, long time to get all the parts build 
without errors using elipse.

To demonstrate the problem I have created a testcase using 6 projects.  

Here are the steps using Eclipse:

0)  Turn off Automatic build on Windows->Perferences

1)  Create the projects:
	CycleDB
	CycleMain
	CyclePeople
	CyclePolicy
	CycleServer
	CycleUtil

2)  Import from the file system into CycleDB the following:
	ivjdab.jar
	vajAS400ET.jar
	vajrmi.jar
	dax.jar
    Import from the file system into CycleServer the following:
	VAJSQLJ.jar

    The jars files are in RTJars.zip	
 
3)  Import the java source into each project from the corresponding jars files 
(which are in Cycle.zip).
    Ensure that the .classpath file is replaced during the import. 

4)  Select Project->Rebuild All

The result will be a few hundred build errors.

Here are the steps using JAVAC:

1) Ensure you have a 1.3 JDK installed

2) Place the bld.cmd (which is in Cycle.zip) in the Eclpise workspace directory

3) From the command line remove all the class files in the workspace directory 
tree
   (for example issue del *.class /s from the workspace directory)

4) Ensure JAVAC is on your path

5) Run bld.cmd
 
The result is a successful build with no errors.

The zip files Cycle and RTJars are available on request.

title: Viewer should delegate equals and hashCode to content provider (1G2PK1A)
description:
The standard viewers are using equals to find a given element in its internal 
data structure
	(for example to find the element that is effected by a domain change). 
This implementation
	leads to some problems in the desktop (see PR. 1G2NSZD: ITPJUI:ALL - 
Got walkback while 
	deleting multiple projects). To solve this problem the viewer should 
delegate equals and
	hashCode for elements to the content provider.

	Note, that the viewer is using a hastable to mantain a fast mapping 
between an element
	and an UI item. So the hashtable must delegate equals and hashCode to 
the content
	provider too. 


NOTES:

	See also:
		 1G47UOR: ITPJUI:WINNT - NullPointerException deleting a project

EG (3/5/01 2:55:37 PM)
	The above PR (1G47UOR) will show-up more frequently when we are self 
hosting.

NE (4/3/01 12:13:27 PM)
	The problem is that viewers do not properly handle multiple equal 
objects.
	In particular, AbstractTreeViewer.updateChildren() causes a 
NullPointerException if there are two equal siblings in the tree.
	Delegating hashcode and equals would not solve this problem, since you 
could still have cases where there are two equal objects
	in the viewer.
	For viewers to properly handle multiple equal objects, we would need to 
make the following changes:
		1. - change findItem and doFindItem to return multiple matching 
objects, and process all matching items on updates
			- element map would have to map from element to Item[]
				- could optimize, and only use array if there 
are multiples
		2. - don't use a Set in AbstractTreeViewer.updateChildren()
		- possibly other places
	At this stage, no API changes are allowed, including changes to 
protected methods, so we would have to be careful here for [1].
	[2] could stil be done without affecting APIs.

DB (04.04.2001 09:34:02)
	The problem we have reported is a little bit different. We have two 
elements in a tree viewer for which element1.equals(element2) returns
	true although they aren't equal in a UI sense (the two elements have 
different parent nodes). Returning true for equals makes totally sense
	from a Java Model perspective, so we can't change the implementation of 
equals.

	Delegating equals and hashCode to the content provider would solve the 
problem for this case. Currently I am not aware of a case where we
	need support for two "UI equal" siblings in a tree or two equal 
elements in a list. So I find it pratical to not supporting this case.

EG (4/4/01 12:58:45 PM)
	Support for multiple equal objects also affects the setUseHashlookup 
mechanism. As DB has pointed out
	having multiple equal objects in the tree isn't the problem, the 
problem is that the client can't define
	the equality criteria. Support for multiple equal children should not 
be added at this point in time. 
	Support for controlling different equality criteria is important. 

NE (04/04/01 9:43:09 AM)
	I have seen errors due to multiple equal children.  It's not a normal 
case, but there was apparently a problem with Java indexing,
	resulting in types showing up twice.  When shown in the hierarchy view, 
AbstractTreeViewer.updateChildren() caused a NPE
	due to improperly handing duplicates.

	For different equality criteria, I recommend simply wrappering the 
objects that cause you problems, and handling the mapping
	in the content provider.

EG (4/4/01 5:15:55 PM)
	The type hierarchy problem your are refering to is a program error. We 
have to fix
	the underlying problem. There is no requirement to show this inconsitent
	state to the user.
	
	"Simply wrappering" the objects is not an option. 
	It is expensive and NOT simple. Keep in mind that notifications have to 
be mapped
	back from model object to wrappers. Selections have to be mapped from 
wrappers back to
	model objects so that the actions work. There is the issue of identity 
leaking etc.
	This is error prone and we went down this path before (see LeapFrog) 
and we
	don't want to go there again. Finally, it was an explicit goal of JFace 
to not require
	clients to wrapper model objects.

NE (4/4/01 2:29:39 PM)
	I need to understand your concrete case better.  Where exactly do you 
run into problems in the Java UI with the current stuff?
	Is it the way two different projects can refer to the same external zip 
or jar?

	If you have two equal model elements showing up in the same viewer, why 
do you want to consider them as different?
	Any change to the model element will require updating all occurrences 
in the viewer (which we don't currently do, but should).
	If you split them up via different equality criteria, you would need to 
manage this yourselves.

	If the element has different containment in the model, then why doesn't 
its equals method reflect this?
	If it's not the element itself which defines different containment, but 
the content provider, 
	how will you be able to impose different equality criteria if there's 
nothing about the elements which distinguishes them?

	Basically, my position is: if we're using the tree viewer as a kind of 
graph viewer, with multiple paths to the same model element,
	then the tree viewer should handle this properly, and it's not clear 
that redefining equals and hashcode is the answer.
	This shouldn't impact the API, except for the assumption that each 
element has a single parent.

EG (4/6/01 10:55:29 AM)
	We are not using the tree views as a graph viewer.
	The problem has to do with external JARs.
	External JARs are shared internally by the JavaModel via some handle 
indirection.
	The UI get's distinct objects for each external JAR, these objects know 
their parent
	etc. However, the JavaModel has decided to forward the equal call to 
the handle body.
	This is OK. This illustrates that hash and equals are context dependent.
	The UI has another understanding what equals and hash means.
	For this reason it should be possible to redefine equals and hash in a 
	context specific way. 

	Side note: hard coding a single equals and hash definition is a general 
problem. The
	Java collection class suffer from the same problem.

	Allowing tree viewers to act as kind of graph viewers would fix this 
specific problem.
	However, this is a significant change compared forwarding equals and 
hash.
	Are the old JFace unit tests up and running so that you could verify the
	consequences of the change?

NE (4/6/01 11:08:50 AM)
	Yes, we revived the old JFace unit tests.

	I understand that delegating equality and hashCode is sometimes 
something you want to do, particularly in general collection libraries.
	(As a side note, the HashTable implementation in .NET allows you to 
plug in an IComparer (for equals) and and IHashCodeProvider (for hashCode)).
	However, as you point out, Java's collection libraries do not support 
this.
	In order to do this in viewers, we would need to add this support by 
subclassing HashMap.
	Unfortunately, this is not straightforward since they both use equals() 
on keys from within a private nested class for entries.
	We would probably have to create our own hashtable .

	This is a non-trivial change to apply to all viewers, and would be an 
API breaking change (if we added the delegation to IContentProvider,
	although we could probably minimize breakage by adding new protocol to 
ContentViewer (e.g. setEqualityDelegate(IEqualityDelegate)).

	For the current problem with external jar elements, is it possible to 
simply change hashCode and equals in the external jar element 
	to include the parent?  After all, it seems to be a distinguishing 
characteristic of the element.

	If not, I will add support for delegating equals and hashcode.  But 
it's a non-trivial change and there are probably more important PRs to address.

	Alternatively, you could subclass TreeViewer and add this support 
yourselves.  You would need to override:
		from StructuredViewer: setUseHashLookup, usingElementMap, 
mapElement and unmapElement, unmapAllElements and findItem
		from AbstractTreeViewer: internalFindItem and internalFindChild
	You need your own hashtable implementation, hang onto it in your own 
instance variable, and change all equals() occurrences 
	in these methods to delegate.

EG (5/4/01 12:34:06 PM)
	check with PM whether hash and equals on external JARs could be changed 
so that the equality check for an external JAR
	also considers its containing project. 

PM (5/4/2001 12:47:04 PM)
	The reason for sharing the JAR entries in the Java model is that it is 
likely that in a multi-project workspace, every single project will refer
	to rt.jar on its classpath, and thus we do not want to maintain 
multiple copies of its elements (given it is the same file underneath).
	Same applies to internal jars. When sharing a reference to a JAR file, 
the elements are shared underneath (given the model implementation 
	used a Map for caching infos (keyed by handled), then this drives our 
implementation of #equals and #hashCode). I would not change this
	assumption this late in the game.

	Couldn't you use mementos instead ? As for defining our own hashtable, 
look at org.eclipse.jdt.internal.compiler.util.HashtableOf...
	implementations which are safe (they are not synchronized thus faster) 
to get inspiration from.

EG (6/2/2001 12:16:10 AM)
	no PRs have shown up because of this, moving to inactive

title: Process.getInputStream().ready() never succeeds
RetargetTextEditorAction ignores accelerators
description:
The accelerators for the RetargetTextEditorActions are not set explictly and 
therefore fail when translations occur. 

They depend on an old 1.0 API that only works in English. Currently the labels 
and accelerators are set using Action.setText(). For the sake of backwards 
compatibility setText will take any text after the @ and attempt to determine 
an accelerator from it comparing with the English words. If those words are not 
in English the accelerator is not set.

In the case of Code Assist for instance the Text in English ends with 
@Ctrl+Space and the text in German with @Stng+Leer. The German string will not 
set an accelerator.

In the specification for actions you can set the accelerator explictly using 
the accelerator tag. The RetargetTextEditorAction should do the same thing.

Marked as P1 critical at Nick Edgars request as accelerators do not work on 
most European locales as a result of this problem.

title: [CVS UI] accessibility issues (1GK7A0R)
description:
These are some notes JM and I made with regard to VCM accessibility.  See also
	1GK79UB: ITPUI:WINNT - Compare FW accessibility issues

Synchronize view issues:
	* The tree nodes in the synchronize view need to expose their state (i.e., incoming, 
	   outgoing, or conflicting), and their type (file or folder).  Currently this information is 
	   only contained in the icon.  Screen readers don't know how to decode this information.
	* Hotkeys for traversing to next and previous difference are not documented
	* When traversing through changes, an audible beep indicates end of file... 	
		may be a hearing-impaired issue.

File compare/replace dialog:
	* spontaneous focus switching
	* no access to toolbar
	* button actions don't have hotkeys
	* scrolling through version list with keyboard is painful, because for each version 
		selected it invokes a server round-trip.

Merge wizard:
	* no widget has initial focus, can't do anything without first clicking in dialog (same 
		as import/export wizards).

title: EC DCR: Why do torn-off views always stay on top? (1GLC4ZM)
description:
From EC post: "Why do torn-off views always stay on top?" by Simon Archer on Oct. 4, 2001.

When you tear-off a view so that it floats outside of a Perspective it
insists on floating on-top of all other Eclipse views.  Does anyone else
find this annoying?

I'd like to be able to tear-off a view and have it fall behind the main
Eclipse window.

Are there any reasons for this not being an option?


NOTES:

NE (10/9/01 11:28:03 AM)
It has to do with them being created as child shells of the window, rather
than being top-level windows in their own right.
This allows Eclipse UI and the underlying window system to manage them
together.
e.g. menu and toolbar of the main window apply to detached views; minimizing
main window also minimizes detached views

However, torn off views do tend to obscure the main window.

I've filed a feature request:
1GLC4ZM: ITPUI:WIN2000 - EC DCR: Why do torn-off views always stay on top?

title: Some Viewers update label decorators very slowly
description:
3 of the JDT viewers update labels very slowly when they get a 
labelProviderChanged event from the DecoratorManager.

using the large workbench provided for Bug 10903 the following ContentViewers 
took a large amount of time to process labelProviderChanged for a very simple 
decorator (I have one that appends the currentTimeMilliseconds to the label and 
does nothing to the image).

ProblemTreeViewer (sometimes upwards of 500 ms)
JavaOutlineViewer (around 200 ms)
MethodsViewer (around 200ms)

This can potentially cause a large delay in update due to the amount of updates 
being sent by the CVS decorator (see Bug 12315).

title: [Modules] CVS checkout of module fails
description:
If a module in CVS is using the "module within a module" syntax in the
CVSROOT/modules file such as

module_name &build &src

where "module_name" is the name of the module and "build" and "src" are folders
within the CVS repository, the checkout fails with a success report.  Eclipse
claims that the module is up to date when in fact no files have been checked
out.  This error only occurs when using the CVS Repository view with the feature
"Checkout as...".  It does not seem to be a problem when starting a new project
from a CVS Repository location.

To reproduce:
1. Create a CVS module using the "module within a module" syntax
2. Create a blank project in Eclipse
3. Using the CVS Repository view, attempt to checkout a module using "Checkout
module as..." and select the newly created project as the parent folder.
4. Receive the message that the module is up to day, when in fact no files have
been checked out.

title: [Presentations] Provide API for querying for physical view bounds
description:
In some cases it would be nice to have an API for finding which view is to the left, right, north, 
south position of a certain other view. (The information seem to be used when dragging and 
dropping views in order to render the correct arrows and dropping the views correctly)

I have 
not been able to find the physical view bounds through the API, only by down-casting views to their 
concrete class and then find their "viewpart"'s window boundaries - not a good thing :(

My 
particular use case is for providing "geographical" navigation actions, so the user can just 
navigate in the direction of the view instead of through Ctrl-F7/Ctrl-F6 like functionallity.

title: New Refactoring: Convert Static Class to Instance [refactoring]
description:
Hi-

We have a lot of classes that shouldn't be static.  It would be create if there
were a refactoring that could take a static class and make it an instance class.
 Basically, all callers to static methods (MyObject.someMethod()) would be
replaced with a call to "new MyObject().someMethod()".  

Ideally the refactoring would be smart enough such that if there were two calls
to the static class in one method, it would create a local variable in the
callers so only one instance of MyObject would be created.

It would also be nice if you could select which methods remain static and which
ones become instance methods.

Adam

title: [RCP] [DnD] Extract EditorInput drag'n'drop from EditorAreaDropAdapter out of org.eclipse.ui.ide plugin
description:
Dragging EditorInputData into the editor area using EditorInputTransfer is a
general functionality that is not specific to an IDE. However part of this
functionality is now implemented inside
org.eclipse.ui.internal.ide.EditorAreaDropAdapter which makes it impossible to
use it in an RCP application without either having a dependency on
org.eclipse.ui.ide or copying the implementation.
This class should be refactored so that the functionality concerning
EditorInputTransfer is moved into a base class available outside
org.eclipse.ui.ide plugin (probably in org.eclipse.ui.workbench plugin?).

because all the data must reside on the server.  I would like to re-use the
generic search facility, however there are a number of references to file based
searches.  File based searches to not make sense for this particular application
because of the database storage system.

not make sense for this application.

framework without requiring me to bundle text & file searches as well.

framework to not show the text search functionality.

2) make some changes to the file, don't save
3) File->export (file system)
4) select the java file you were editing, export to your desktop
5) open the java file, note that your changes are not in the file

	assert(fMB1.subtract(fMB1).isNull()); 

	2) hit <ctrl>-h
	3) The search dialog opens
	4) observe: the "type" radio button is checked, even though this is clearly a method

	As I understand it, we have a heuristic guessing the kind of expression to search for.
	Shouldn't it pick up this case?

DM (6/5/01 7:03:04 PM)
	Search uses code resolve form Java Model. Unfortunately code resolve does not
	include the arguments i.e. the text selection "assert" will be
	resolved and lead to the expected result (i.e. method selected in search dialog)
	while assert(...) wont.

	If we want to have code resolve working on the whole method then Java Model's
	code resolve should offer this.

	Please note that the whole Java UI always selected the method name excluding
	the arguments. Also double click selects only the name i.e. if you double click
	on assert then assert without the args is selected and CTRL+H will work as expected.

title: [Operations] Remote tag should batch as much as possible
description:
When tagging files via the repository view, files from multiple repositories,
projects, and tags can be selected. In order to allow this behavior, the
TagInRepositoryOperation loops over all resources and tags them individually.
This works correctly, but generates considerably more CVS traffic than is necessary.

As a result of the loop, every resource results in a separate hit to the
associated CVS servers. Because of these separate hits, multiple taginfo events
are also generated on the server. Software that uses taginfo events to fire
programs or log information about CVS access end up handling multiple events. I
my case, the CVS server ends up sending an email for each file tagged.

TagInRepositoryOperation should be modified to batch CVS hits by repository and
source tag. This would be sufficient separation to allow the current behavior of
the repository view to work correctly, but would allow multiple tag operations
against the same repository and tag to be sent to the server as a single operation.

I have part of this work under way now, but would like comments.
