title: [Progress] [Properties] [Preference] Property/Preference pages should use a common operation/progress monitor
description:
We have added several pages to the Properties dialog, and a lot of these can
potentially modify the workspace.  Unfortunately, under the current
implementation, hitting OK in the Properties dialog after changing a few
pages means that each page will launch its own ProgressMonitorDialog, do its
thing, and then build and/or validate the project.  The biggest disadvantage
is that the project is being built/validated several times, which can be a
time-consuming process.  Having several progress dialogs pop up is also a 
usability concern.

I have noticed that the Preferences dialog has the same problem.  You can do
the following to see the problem:
1)  Go to Java -> Compiler and change one of the options that would cause it
re-compile all project in the workspace.
2) Without hitting Apply or OK, go to Plug-in Development -> Compilers and
change another option there that can cause it to re-compile all projects as 
well.
Now, when you hit OK, it will try to re-compile all the projects twice.

So, as a solution to this problem, I propose that the Property/Preferene 
dialogs use a WorkspaceModifyComposedOperation when invoking performOk() on all 
pages and pass an IProgressMonitor, that can be shared by all the methods, as a 
parameter to that method.

title: [KeyBindings] registry: acceleratorSets don't work in 3.0
description:
I have realized that acceleratorSets didn't work in 3.0.  They are not parsed
correctly by the Persistence class.

The acceleratorSets extension point was introduced in 2.0, and deprecated in
2.1.   It has been replaced with the commands extension point.  The extension
point was parsed correctly in 2.1.x and earlier.

I believe there are three separate options.
1.) Go back to the 2.1.x code and find the acceleratorSets parsing code.  Copy
it into 3.1.
2.) Remove the acceleratorSets extension point and mark it as a breaking change
in 3.1.
3.) Leave the extension point, but leave do not provide any code to parse it. 
Wait for someone to complain.


My general impression is to go for (2).  There are no bugs filed about its
absence yet, and my feeling is that no one misses it.  By removing the extension
point, anyone who happens to use it would see compiler errors.  The note about
breaking changes would give people using it a pointer as to where they should
look.  (As a note, it does not break binary compatibility -- referencing
extension points that don't exist does not cause errors at run-time.)


For now, I'm going implement (3), and wait for some more input on this bug.

title: Need an API to open multiple editors side by side
description:
I have been discussing this feature request thru Julian Jones with OTI. This 
feature request is to formalize it.

In our XSL debugger, we would like to see the XSL source and the XML source 
together (side by side), so that when we single step thru, it will highlight 
the line in the XSL source editor and the corresponding line in the XML source 
editor.

Right now there is no programatic way to open the editors and position them 
side by side. The user has to manually drag one editor and drop it to the edge 
of the WB window.

Would like an API to do it. Also would be nice if the settings can be 
remembered, and if the same source can be stacked together. That is, if 2 XML 
source and 2 XSL source are needed, the XML sources stacked behind each other, 
and the XSL sources stacked together.

But if I can just get the API to position them side by side in 2.0, I will 
already be very happy.

title: Import: Select Type does not select anything  (1GGYV3Z)
description:
id  RATLC00009823     Priority: 2
Headline:  Import: Select Type does not select anything 
  
 Description:  In the import wizard, the Select Type button does not select anything. 

STEPS TO REPLICATE: 
- select File->Import 
- select File System for import source and press Next 
- enter a directory with subfolders and files (eg. WINNT) 
- press Select Types 
- in the Select Types dialog, press Select All and press OK 

Result: 
- Nothing was selected in main wizard

 NOTE: Select Types only filters the selected files if all the files were already selected.

ARCH (7/18/01 7:04:25 PM)
	Investigate for 1.0.
	Fix only if trivial.

existing selections and will not query files that are not selected for efficiency reasons.

would be less confusing

	A better solution is to make Select Types actually select the chosen types.
	Since this may lead to significant work by the UI, it should use a cancelable progress monitor
	(also for Select All case, or even checking individual items).

title: inline method - breaks code when inlining methods with try catch blocks [refactoring]
on-the-fly check for errors should wait until you stop typing
description:
Currently, the on-the-fly error checker runs after every keystroke. This makes typing horribly 
slow when dealing with large files (>1000 lines), and I usually end up having to disable it.

It 
would be better if the checker waited for me to stop typing before running. This would be good for 
two reasons: better performance, and I don't care about errors while I'm typing (I'm not done the 
statement yet!). This would be done by starting a reseting a timer after every keystroke, and only 
running the checker once the timer fires. Preferrably the interval of the timer would be user 
definable.

This is how JBuilder does it, and I found it to work quite well.

mapping of open documents to split panes to be persisted on shutdown.

title: API - step filters should be configurable per target
description:
Currently step filters are global to the java debug plug-in. In the interest of 
a more flexible API, step filters should be configurable per debug target. The 
preference store should be kept with the java debug UI.

For example, this would allow step filters to be specified as part of a launch 
configuration. In the case of a super adapter, this would allow the adapter to 
control step filtering in its underlying target, without effecting stand-alone 
debug sessions.

title: Text Editor Smoke Tests (1GHFZ95)
description:
This is a test list for the text editor.

Presentation
	Verify that appropriate strings appear in all menu items and text fields.
	Verify that the view shows appropriate scrollbars when its contents extends beyond its client area.

Editor Actions
	Verify that Cut and Copy are enabled iff there is selected text.
	Verify that Paste is enabled iff there is text in the clipboard buffer.
	Verify that Cut, Copy, Paste, Select-All work correctly.
	Verify that Revert is enabled only if is the file dirty and works correctly.

Edit Menu Actions
	Verify that the enablement and action of Cut, Copy, Paste, and Select-All in the Edit menu are consistent with those in the editor's context menu.

Persistence	
	The editor is marked dirty if the text is modified by either the keyboard OR the editor actions.
	The editor is marked clean after either saving the file or reverting it.

title: [Decorators] Decorator mechanism does not allow for optimizations
description:
At present our decorators show up piecemeal because we do them in a background 
thread and thus the order they appear is 'random'.

The way we decorator mechanism works does not allow us to optimize in some 
areas.  Specificly:

1. The icon and text are asked for separately. This requires us to go to our 
sync info twice, which is on disk and expensive to get.

2. The decorators are asked individually.  In the case of CVS, all the sync 
info for sibling resources is in the same file, so its faster for us to 
determine all their decorators at once.

3. In order to avoid doing work in the UI thread, we create a background thread 
to generate the decorators.  When then need to tell the UI via an event that we 
now have decorators, and then they ask us for them.  It would be better if we 
could just give the UI the decorators we know about all at once.

Note: to be a good citizen we should be computing the decorators in a thread 
different than the UI context.

The combination of #2 and #3 could result in the decorators appearing in parent 
child ordering, with all siblings appearing at once.

title: Adding a bookmark should open the Bookmarks View (1GE8I5C)
description:
When you add a bookmark either to a file or a location within a file, it would make
sense to open the Bookmarks View if it is not already open (without giving it focus).
This would be especially useful when in the Java Perspective as the Bookmarks View is
not one of default views, but this also applies to bookmarking in any Perspective.

1) create a new Java Project
2) add a new class to the project
3) open the class in the editor (double click)
4) right click in the margin of the editor and select "Add Bookmark"
5) give the bookmark a name

Here you see the bar icon appear in the margin to indicate the bookmark.
To reference your bookmark however, you need to do the following:

menu: Perspective->Show View->Other...[Expand 'Basic'->Bookmarks]

If the auto-open Bookmarks is implemented, it is important not to give it focus,
we don't want to interrupt the user when he adds a bookmark.  By opening the view
a new user will know how to reference her bookmarks.

title: [Commands] CVS ignores linked resources
description:
Steps to recreate seem to be the best way to describe this issue:
1. Create a project in the workspace
2. Create a folder in the new project, link the folder using linked resources to
a directory in the file system.
3. Checkout a module from CVS into the folder created above.
(At this point, I can do a "Synchronize with repository" on the project and the
result is, as expected, a message saying that there are no differences.)
4. Exit the Eclipse.
5. Start the Eclipse.
6. Check the properties of the project, the CVS information looks ok.
7. Check the properties of the folder, and the CVS section of the Properties
dialog says "This folder has lost its sharing information"

If the folder created in step 2 was not a linked folder but a folder right under
the project folder, the CVS sharing information doesn't get lost.

I have chosen the severity of this issue as "critical" because at this moment,
if I want to use Eclipse's CVS functionality, I can't keep files from/for CVS
out of the workspace directory.

Build used is 20030806

title: [View Mgmt] Make view navigation more accesible
description:
Have you ever tried Intellij Idea's Java IDE ?  If you have, you know how much good keyboard support 
can do for your "workflow" :)

I suggest that Eclipse UI team should take a good look at Idea and 
its way of handling its "views" - especially the way they are easily hidden, but still shown in the 
side with a number, indicating which key to press together with "Alt" to display it again. Eclipse 
is ofcourse build to have many views, though one might make it possible to assign a shortcut to 
certain views or even better just assign a unique number to each view, which is the number that one 
have to enter when you press Alt. Or why stop at numbers, how about being able to assign just any kind 
of key or sequence of keys. e.g. Alt + e + l would give me the "Error Log".

Another great 
enhancment would be to be able to cycle the between views/editors both internally in a panegroup 
and between panegroups with the arrow keys. 
e.g. If I have 5 editors open and the cursor is the 
first one the Alt + rightarrow would shift to the editor tab to the right and so forth. This Alt + 
arrowkeys could be generally applied to everything with a tab in eclipse.
This solves the 
somewhat not-so-quick Ctlr-F6 editor navigation.

Navigation between the group of 
editors/views could also be very easy by using e.g. Shift + Alt + arrowkeys to navigate to the view 
that is nearest in a certain direction. This allows me to use the screen to navigate, instead of 
forcing me to remember which specific key a specific view is assigned to.

All this combined 
with a history of navigations which could quickly be traversed e.g. by Ctlr + Alt + arrowkeys (very 
much like it is done in Intellij Idea)

From: "Nick Edgar" <nick_edgar@oti.com>
Subject: Re: navigator view context menu contribution
Date: Wednesday, May 30, 2001 3:00 PM

We currently have no plans to change this.

The problem is that the only way you're going to get rich enough conditions
for enablement is to allow arbitrary Java code to be run.
Which means activating the plugin just to determine whether the action is
enabled or not.
Eclipse tries very hard to avoid starting plugins unnecessarily, to keep
startup time down.
E.g., if I'm editing text and not editing HTML, it should not have to
activate any part of the HTML plugin.

title: DCR - Spacebar does not toggle checkbox state (1GEA975)
[Workbench] Need support for editor-less resources
description:
At present, resources are expected to be associated with editors.  Specifying an editor for a file 
extension is the only way to associate an icon with a resource, and double clicking a resource 
always opens an editor on the resource, even if no editor has been specified.  We need to provide 
support for resources in the workspace that do NOT have associated editors.  At a minimum, this 
means some way  to specify icons for them, and some way to intercept the double-click action and do 
something other than open an editor on the resource.  The current use-case for this is launch 
configurations, which are XML files that are maintained through the 
LaunchConfigurationDialog (not an editor).

title: font changes (1GJ6N1E)
description:
This is a tracking PR to use JFace FontRegistry and one of the 4 supported font aliases 
	(BANNER_FONT, DIALOG_FONT, TEXT_FONT, TERMINAL_FONT).
	See email for more details.


NOTES:
	BF (2001/08/28 15:49:36)
		Moving to Inbox for version 2.0

	e-mail:
		Scripting is changed to use default fonts (does not set fonts).
		So unless we see a really compelling reason to change I would recommend
		just moving the PR to InBox for 2.0.
		Using the TERMINAL_FONT in the source view may be the only place where
		we may want to make a change in the 1.0 stream (but I even question that at this point).

		There is no new API added. The JFace font registry has public API. We are adding one new font alias for
		a fixed width font and the workbench is going to provide a preference page.
		Your code would need to get it's font's from the JFace registry and listen to font change events.

		You can continue to use your own fonts if you really have to. However, it would be better if the platform
		had a single preference page for configuring the fonts. This will also make your NL and accesability work easier
		as you can rely on the workbench to give you an appropriate font for all locales.

		What would need to change in the font aliases to enable you to avoid defining your own fonts? If we can come up
		with a generic name for the font we can add it now.

		There is a font registry already defined in the workbench unfortunately for ISV's there was NO user interface to
		allow the user to change the default fonts. The font properties file currently defines entries for the following fonts:

		BANNER_FONT
		DIALOG_FONT
		DEFAULT_FONT
		VIEWER_FONT
		WINDOW_FONT
		TEXT_FONT

		We are going to discourage the use of  VIEWER_FONT and WINDOW_FONT as there isn't a clear mapping
		between these fonts and what the user expects. The notion of DEFAULT_FONT is not necessary (as you will see later).

		We are adding a fixed with font alias as well. It is expected that PDE will  use this. Investigation of WSAD
		suggests that they could also use a fixed width font.

		BANNER_FONT - Used in the wizard and dialog banner. By default this is a bold font
		DIALOG_FONT - Used in dialogs. (e.g. Text messages in Wizards)
		TEXT_FONT - Default text font
		TERMINAL_FONT - Default fixed width font.

title: [Dialogs] workbench progress indicator may be hidden by modal dialogs
description:
I came across some code that used the workbench's progress indicator for a long-
running operation as follows:

    // Run the operation
    PlatformUI.getWorkbench().getActiveWorkbenchWindow().run(true,false,buOp);

The problem is that this code was run while a modal Properties dialog was up.  
If the dialog happened to be covering the part of the workbench window with the 
status bar/progress indicator in it, the user might be unaware that something 
was happening/progress was being made.

If the code *knows* it is run while a modal dialog is up, it can create a 
ProgressMonitorDialog and use that instead.  However, there are (several?) 
cases where some shared, supporting code needs to do a long-running operation, 
and may not know whether the operation is requested in a modal or
non-modal context.  One example of such a situation is when I click 
a "Browse..." button inside a dialog, and the platform has to go and find the 
things I'm going to browse.  Even if the code does know whether it was called 
in a modal or non-modal user context, it needs to have code for both behaviors.

I talked about this with James Moody and we can't think of any situations where 
the workbench progress bar is better than a ProgressMonitorDialog if the user 
is in a modal context/dialog.

Therefore: Make this an explicit policy.  The workbench should do it in one 
place instead of trying to do it in multiple places in client code.

Specifically, when asked to run an operation, the workbench should determine if 
any modal dialog is up and if so, it should create a new ProgressMonitorDialog 
with a generic title etc. and use that for the operation instead of using the 
status bar.

title: DCR: need a way to convert the content of the .log file into IStatus objects (1GCI0VB)
description:
It is currently possible to register with the platform as a log listener. However, logs that
are dispatched are those from the moment of registration. PDE Error Log view needs to
show logs that happened before it was opened. 

An API is needed that parses the current content of the .log file and returns
an array of IStatus objects. PDE Error Log could use it to display logs that
happened from the moment of the workbench startup.

PDE could write a parser itself, but there are two disadvantages to it:

1) PDE does not own the .log file.
2) It is not good to separate code that writes and code that reads the same
file format. Since .log file format is private to the Core, it has the privilage
to change its format without notice. All PDE cares for is to get an array
of IStatus objects.


NOTES:

JM (06/05/2001 11:19:25 AM)
	Clarification needed:  
		- What should happen with the exceptions which are dumped to the
			log?  On parsing/reading the log we are not keen on somehow rebuilding the exception 
			objects.
		- In what form should the returned value be? (Status objects, strings, ...?) 

	Awaiting info...

DG (5/6/2001 11:45:36 AM)
   1) Of course, it would be ideal if rebuilt status objects would not differ from those logged after
   the log view has been activated. However, all I really need is the actual stack dump 
   of the exception, not the exception object ifself. If you could create an IStatus implementation
   that will give me exception text instead of the object, I would be OK.

   2) This is related to 1). Error Log works with IStatus objects, so an array of IStatus objects
   would be ideal. On initialization, Error Log view would ask the Platform to give it all the
   status objects that have been logged until that moment (including those during the boot). 
   These status object will be shown as the initial content of the view. After that new status
   objects will be added on top as they are logged.

   BTW, this feature will allow users to clear the log so that only new status objects are
   seen as they arrive, but also to restore the entire log. For this reason, the method to
   parse the .log file and return status objects may be called even during the lifetime of 
   the Error Log view (each time people press "Restore Logs" button).

title: Product won't start if directory contains !%# (1GIRLOO)
description:
Defect 182384 has been opened by jcagle.

Component   wsa.web.oti
Severity    3
Prefix      p
Release
Reference
Abstract    Product won't start if directory contains !%#
Remarks:

Tested using Eclipse 0.128 build.

The product will not start if the install directory contains an exclamation point (!),
pound (#), or percent (%).

If the directory has a "!", javaw starts and then ends immediately.  If the directory
contains either "%" or "#", eclipse.exe starts but javaw.exe never starts.

This is probably something that we just need to restrict in the install.

Also see defect 182383 for problems if install directory contains "^" or "`".
NOTES:

JM (9/17/2001 1:56:12 PM)

title: DCR - Rendering hints on GC - anti alias / mitre
description:
The SWT GC should support rendering hints on the GC.  By documenting these 
as "hints" application developers are free to take advantage of better graphics 
support on platforms that have them, and on platforms that don't, the graphics 
will degrade in an acceptible fashion to the platform defaults.  For example, 
Windows will support anti-aliased lines, elipses, fills, etc.  Also, you can 
change the mitre of lines and polylines.

This should be exposed in SWT.  In my current project, I am debating whether I 
should use Images to cache the desired anti-alised appearance, and render the 
antialiasing myself.  Or I might store a few decorations as Images because I 
cannot paint those decorations the way I would like.  The end result is that I 
am going to use more Image handles.

title: [DetachedViews] problem moving detached tab group
description:
If I try to drag a detached tab group (using context menu Move>Tab Group) past
'certain limits' the outline box stops moving and the cursor changes from the
box to an arror, and the cursor keeps moving.  If I drop at that point, the
group usually drops where the cursor was, not where the box froze.  I have
multiple monitors and this seems to happen only on one of them, and only on the
left and lower portions of the screen - when the position becomes very negative
from the origin on the primary monitor, e.g. -3000 in the horizontal axis or
-1000 in the vertical axis.  This problem does not occur when dragging a single
view by grabbing the view tab in the main eclipse window with the mouse.  It
also does not occur when dragging a detached tab group around by grabbing the
title bar with the mouse.

The above behavior occurs virtually all the time.

In one single case (which I have not been able to reproduce) a more stateful and
confusing behavior occured.  I moved the cursor past the point where the drag
outline box froze, and released the mouse button.  The drag outline remained
frozen on the screen.  I grabbed the title bar of the detached group and moved
it somewhere else, which appeared to work.  The drag outline remained on the
screen.  Now the odd part - whenever I moved the mouse (with no buttons down)
into the screen area of the detached tab group, the outline box 'reactivated'
and began following the mouse around (leaving some droppings in various places)
as long as the mouse stayed within the window boundaries of the detached group.
 If I moved the mouse outside the window, the box froze at that point.  I
clicked inside the window and the window moved to that location, the everything
reverted to normal.

title: Need to get full set of breakpoints hit from thread.
description:
When creating super adapters on top of the Java debug adapter we set hidden 
temporary breakpoints in order to control the Java debug adapter.  If the user 
also sets a breakpoint at the same spot as one of our temporary breakpoints then 
when we get a suspend event due to a breakpoint from the Java thread we need to 
be able to ask the thread for the list of breakpoints that were hit.  Currently 
we can only get one breakpoint from the thread.  If we only see our temporary 
breakpoint which we might choose to ignore and don't see the user breakpoint 
then we will run away.

title: Compare editor not restored on startup (1GH4I27)
description: The compare editor does not survive shutdown and startup. Sometimes compares are quite large and may take a while to peruse. It should save its state like the other editors and views. NOTES: JEM (9/13/2001 10:56:28 AM) We can persist the state of the editor, but it will still have to re-perform the compare. The persistence happens via getPersistable() of the CompareEditorInput object. (For example, the persistable could remember the local project and the team stream element that were being compared). The compare editor will still re-perform the comparation based on that input when the editor opens. But this behaviour is better than the current behaviour of nothing. This is equivalent to the behaviour of other editors, where the text editor remembers the name of the file it was editing, but upon re-creation it still has to go and re-discover the content from disk. JEM (9/13/2001 2:43:37 PM) The general compare framework would also need to be fixed. From CompareEditorInput: /** * Returns null since this editor cannot be persisted. * * @return null because this editor cannot be persisted */ public IPersistableElement getPersistable() { return null; } JEM (9/14/2001 10:47:34 AM) Logged JUI PR 1GK1SLZ: ITPJUI:WIN2000 - Compare editor not restored on startup

title: [ViewMgmt] View label changes are not being picked up
description:
There is a problem that has occured while building on top of Eclipse plugins.
I have isolated the problem and was able to re-create it using PDE-Example.
Scenario:
1. Create a Hello World Sample (Plug-in Project with a View) inside the PDE 
environment perspective.
2. A plugin project should be created with plugin.xml and the extension point 
for the view looks something like this:
   <extension
         point="org.eclipse.ui.views">
      <category
            name="Sample Category"
            id="HelloWorld">
      </category>
      <view
            name="Sample View"
            icon="icons/sample.gif"
            category="HelloWorld"
            class="HelloWorld.views.SampleView"
            id="HelloWorld.views.SampleView">
      </view>
   </extension>

3. Create a plugin.properties file in the plugin project with the following 
entry:
Helloworld.sample = Sample View 100
4. Now update the extension point for the view in plugin.xml file with this:
   <extension
         point="org.eclipse.ui.views">
      <category
            name="Sample Category"
            id="HelloWorld">
      </category>
      <view
            name="%Helloworld.sample"
            icon="icons/sample.gif"
            category="HelloWorld"
            class="HelloWorld.views.SampleView"
            id="HelloWorld.views.SampleView">
      </view>
   </extension>

Note: The name for the view is referencing the key in the properties file.
5. Now Bring up the Runtime workbench and you should see the Sample View 100 by
going to Window --> Show View --> Other... --> Sample Category --> Sample View 
100 click on it and bring up this Sample View 100.
6. Now bring down the runtime workkbench
7. Change the value in the plugin.properties file as follows and save:
Helloworld.sample = Sample View 200
8. Bring up the workbench and the Sample View 100 is seen but not the Sample 
View 200 as the property has been changed in the plugin.properties
9. Tried a variation now by changing the plugin.xml extension point as follows 
and it worked once when I re-bring up the workbench:
   <extension
         point="org.eclipse.ui.views">
      <category
            name="Sample Category"
            id="HelloWorld">
      </category>
      <view
            name="Sample View 300"
            icon="icons/sample.gif"
            category="HelloWorld"
            class="HelloWorld.views.SampleView"
            id="HelloWorld.views.SampleView">
      </view>
   </extension>
10. But now if I repeat step 4, I would see it still works and I see "Sample 
View 200" as specified in the properties file.
11. Now if I repeat step 7 and change the value in the properties file to
Helloworld.sample = Sample View 400
and bring up the workbench it again fails to pick up the Sample View 400 but 
stays at Sample View 200.

I know the problem seems to be a little tricky to reproduce, I tried to explain 
it as clearly as I could, if there are any other questions please feel free to 
contact me.
We need this name of the view in plugin.properties as we need the name of the 
view to be transalted.
Hoping to hear back from some one soon. Thanks.

title: Not implemented error messages in Slider and others
description:
In SWT/Win, Slider.setEnabled() has a line of code as follows:

if (OS.IsWinCE) error (SWT.ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED);

The problem with this logic is that it requires all senders to catch exceptions 
whereever any possible unimplemented API exists.  This is prohibitive to do for 
all API, since anything is possibly unimplemented on platform <X>.  There are 
other occurrences of code like the above, mostly in Slider (one non-Slider 
example is Button.computeSize()).

We would prefer this to simply return silently, much like the approach taken in 
Menu.setDefaultItem().

title: Confirm project delete dialog could be enhanced
description:
The new project delete dialog (as in build 2002-01-15) improved on the previous 
one so as to ask whether to delete the contents of the project in the file 
system.

However, the dialog is a bit too verbose. It would be better if instead of two 
radio buttons, we should only have one check box. It would say:
   Delete contents under <<path to project location>>
or
   Delete contents in the file system
when multiple projects selected.

By default, the check box is not selected. It is obvious enough to the user 
that selecting it will delete the contents, while not selecting it will leave 
the contents alone.

Usability guidelines recommend keeping dialog text brief and to the point. 
Users do not like to read much! Also, only to use two radio buttons instead of 
a check box only if it is not obvious to the user what the check and uncheck 
state will do. In this case, it is obvious and will help keep the dialog brief.

title: Observations on StyledText behavior (1GLEA8Y)
description:
The StyledText line-drawing code may be executed several times.
	Compare the following two cases:

	A.  In a simple stand-alone test case, create a StyledText and setText
() to
	  "blah blah".  Put a trace print in drawStyledLine().  Try inserting 
characters;
	  depending on where the caret is, the method will be executed 2 or 3 
times
	  which looks correct because we are drawing the different parts of the 
string.
	  The feel of the widget is OK.

	B.  When editing a flat file in Eclipse, inserting a character executes 
drawStyledLine()
	  15 times.  When editing Java source, the method executes up to 34 
times.
NOTES:

	BGS (10/10/2001 3:43:05 PM) -
		Q: Why does it have to blank the line first anyway?

	McQ (10/10/2001 3:50:28 PM) -
		I've seen this. It's pretty painful. We need to identify (at 
every level)
		places where we are gratuitously painting multiple times.

		Could the line blanking have anything to do with X buffering?

	KR (10/10/01 4:16:15 PM)
		Where in drawStyledLine did you put the trace? I assume outside 
the loop that iterates
		over the styles. drawStyledLine renders a complete line so if 
you set text it should
		only be called once for each line.
		Maybe you don't notice the slow painting much on Windows 
because 
			a) it is better at merging paints (a guess)
			b) it draws faster (a fact)

		StyledText redraws the line when a character is typed. Eclipse 
uses the setStyleRange API
		to update the styles which in turn does another redraw. These 
two redraws should normally 
		be merged by the OS or by SWT paint merge code on Motif.
		If drawStyledLine is called 15 times for the same line when 
typing one character in a simple 
		file (no syntax coloring) Eclipse is likely doing something 
bogus that causes 15 redraws.
		If I type a character in the SwtStyledTextUseCase 
drawStyledLine is called once, regardless
		of whether Java syntax coloring is turned on or not.	

	BGS (10/10/2001 4:35:45 PM) -
		I put the trace as the very first statement in drawStyledLine
(), so we're talking about the
		number of times drawStyledLine() gets called as a whole.
		Could someone comment on the blanking [erasing] issue?

title: [Help] Missing Help Index Solution
description:
Eclipse does not support building of an alphabetical on-line help index. This 
will be very limiting to the end-user trying to locate relevant help topics.

Requirements of an index:
- offers a simple mechanism by which to access topics based on important 
keywords in the topic, where the keywords are listed as alphabetical entries in 
the index. User picks the index item (a keyword) to open one topic, or access a 
list of relevant topics.
- multiple keywords can map to one topic
- multiple topics can use the same keyword
- index entries can be nested to at least 3 levels
- index entries from each contributing 'book' can be merged into one 
consolidated index for the whole system
- [optional] multiple indexes can be defined and accessed for a system
- [optional] ideally, the user would be able to start typing in field at the 
topic of the index, and have the index scroll automatically (after each letter 
entered or after a short pause) to the location in the index corresponding to 
the letters typed so far.

A short list of arguments for having this mechanism:
- Without an index, the user must find topics by knowing the exact spelling or 
syntax of a word or phrase to seach on, or must know which book and where in 
the table of contents hierarchy to begin looking. With an index, the user can 
begin typing or scroll through a predefined, alphabetical list of terms to 
locate a term just by knowing the first few characters.
- Without an index, the user is left only with a string search mechanism, which 
could potentially return a huge list of topics that reflects every occurrance 
of the string in the help system. With an index, the help system authors can 
intelligently choose the topics that provide the best information for a 
particular term, thus providing the most efficient end-user experience.
- Without an index, the user is unable to see related or extension topics to 
the core term. With an index, related or extension topics can be listed through 
nested entries.

title: Public interface for call hierarchy analysis [call hierarchy]
description:
Hi. I would like to see a public interface for call hierarchy analysis based on 
the work of Jesper Kamstrup Linnet (org.eclipse.jdt.internal.ui.callhierarchy). 
Using this interface, people could plugin other features that use this 
information, providing a different kind of visualization, optimization or 
refactoring.
The interface should provide the following features:
1.) Retrieval of the list of IMethod objects directly being called by a given 
IMethod object. 
2.) Retrieval of the list of IMethod objects which directly call a given 
IMethod object.
Also I had a look at the analysis currently used. It seems that Eclipse is just 
performing an exhaustive search on declared (!) types, which is rather 
incorrect in some cases of virtual method call resolution (for more information 
see http://www.sable.mcgill.ca/publications/papers/#oopsla2000).
So I would also like to see a generic interface of a call graph search and that 
the existing call hierarchy feature uses the factory pattern to plug in a 
search that uses this interface. So additional, more accurate searches, could 
be easily included. For switching these searches, the call hierarchy plugin 
should provide an appropriate selector in the Eclipse preferences.
All this functionality might be implemented using the following public 
interface:

import org.eclipse.jdt.core.ICompilationUnit;
import org.eclipse.jdt.core.IMethod;

/**
 * @author Eric Bodden (eric@bodden.de)
 *
 * Interface AbstractCallGraphSearch
 */
public interface AbstractCallGraphSearch {

	/**
	 * Builds a call graph including nodes of the given compilation units. 
	 * @param toIncludeCompilationUnits Compilation units which methods 
should
	 *        be included in this call graph.
	 */
	public void initCallGraph(ICompilationUnit[] toIncludeCompilationUnits);
	
	/**
	 * Returns the methods that are directly called by the given method.
	 * The exact result set is based on the virtual call resolution of the
	 * analysis.
	 * @param method The parent method. Must be part of one of the 
compilation
	 * 		  units used for the initialization.
	 * @return Methods being direcly called by the method passed as 
parameter.
	 * @exception UnresolvedMethodException Thrown if method is not member 
of the
	 *            set of compilation units used for the initialization.
	 */
	public IMethod[] directCallTargetsOf(IMethod method) throws 
UnresolvedMethodException;

	/**
	 * Returns the methods that directly call the given method.
	 * The exact result set is based on the virtual call resolution of the
	 * analysis.
	 * @param method An arbitrary. Must be part of one of the compilation
	 * 		  units used for the initialization.
	 * @return Methods being direcly called by the method passed as 
parameter.
	 * @exception UnresolvedMethodException Thrown if method is not member 
of the
	 *            set of compilation units used for the initialization.
	 */
	public IMethod[] directCallersOf(IMethod method) throws 
UnresolvedMethodException;
}

In the case of any questions feel free to email me.
Cheers,
Eric

title: Ant Javac task uses the execution runtime to compile (1GF0S3C)
description:
The Javac task (actually the DefaultCompilerAdapter) by default uses the current VM's java.home as the base
for finding the class lib to compile against.  Under java.home it expects to see lib/rt.jar or some such.  For J9 
the lib structure is different (e.g., lib/jclMax/classes.zip).  This means that users cannot compile Java code using
Ant under J9.  

NOTES:

JM (6/8/2001 4:51:53 PM)
	1) the workaround is to move/copy the requires classes.zip file up to where the Ant adapter is expecting it to be.
	This is less than optimal but works.  

	2) The better answer if for us to add the ability to take a "jre" or "jcl" property and use that (if set) to spec the 
	location of the class lib
	
	3) An alternative is to add args to javac to handle the new function.  However this would require retooling the 
	build script generator to include the required values in the javac task

	4) A futher alternative is to create another adapter specificially for J9 and then allow this value to be spec'd when 
	running the ant script.

	Of all of these, #2 seems like the most realistic and flexible.  (of course #1 can be done now by users).  

JM (6/11/2001 2:25:52 PM)
	No action now.  Should consider the options above post-June

AE (9/3/2001 5:38:02 PM)
	I assume that this PR is the result of the problem I had with the PDE.
	The assumption that the run time library is always on $java.home/lib/rt.jar is wrong.

	In org.eclipse.pde.internal.core.JDTCompilerAdapter the following is written:

		 .addExisting(new Path(null, System.getProperty("java.home") + "/lib/rt.jar"));

	this should be:

		 .addExisting(new Path(null, JavaCore.getClasspathVariable("JRE_LIB").toOSString());

	Warning: according to EG classpath variables will become scoped per Java project, and the variable value
	will have to be taken from the PDE project that is being built.

JW (10/4/01 11:50:48 AM)

title: [plan item] Improve local history
description:
Improve local history. The local history mechanism for resources in the 
workspace should be improved. Currently, clients of the IResource API control 
whether snapshot of a modified or deleted file gets captured in the local 
resource history. Unfortunately this makes local history less of a safety net 
than it could be if plug-ins do not use this mechanism properly. Eclipse 
should put in place a system-wide policy for resource history retention. The 
local resource history should also be better integrated with team repository 
providers, and allow users to selectively purge a file's local history when it 
is committed to a team repository. [Platform Core, Platform UI, Platform Team]

title: Enhance SWT's ability to implement IDispatch
description:
It is possible to implement IID_IDispatch instances in SWT using COMObject.  
However, it's not obvious how to do so and the implementer is left with the 
responsibility of cracking all IDispatch method arguments.

Instead, enhance SWT by offering a base implementation of IID_IDispatch that 
cracks arguments and delegates to relevant Java methods.  This would greatly 
ease the burden of implementing IID_IDispatch and would facilitate interaction 
with a great many COM controls including deep integration with Internet 
Explorer.

title: [Properties dialog] Output path error message is easy to miss (1GIF5CW)
description:
I've been creating some self-hosting projects for the UI examples.
I usually go and modify the class path to use a subfolder with the original project name,
so the default output folder isn't acceptable.

It gives me a warning in the title of the property page, but its background is gray.
The text is also often truncated due to the length of the names.
So it's easy to miss when staring at the OK button and wondering why it's disabled.

If you do find the message, it's not obvious how to go about fixing it (especially since it's truncated):
you have to append /bin to the output folder field.

It really took me a while the first time to figure this out, even though I know wizards and dialogs
report errors at the top.

This is probably a general issue with how we report errors in preference and property pages,
so feel free to move down after your consideration.

title: Usability: Script outline has inconsistent selection (1GF5YSQ)
description:
1. Create a file called test.xhtml.  
2. Open it in a script editor.
3. In the outline, click on the body tag.
4. Click on form tag.

Notice how many of the buttons in the editor are enabled.

5. Click on label tag.
6. Click on form tag.

Notice how very few of the buttons in the editor are enabled.

Given that my selection is the same, I do not understand why the state of action
enablement has changed.

NOTES:

DS (6/11/01 12:51:15 PM)
	Ah, now I understand.  The state of the "Add as child" and "Add as SIbling" buttons
	change as you select different items.  I am not convinced that the add mode can be
	derived from the active selection in the tree.   For instance, if I have a table row
	selected do you know if I want to "add a table data child" or "add a table row sibling".
	The UI behavior would probably be more predictable if you do NOT change the
	add mode.  In my own experience with this editor the prediction is wrong about
	50% of the time.

BF (2001/06/11 13:07:40)
	Agreed.  The enabling algorithm is unable to predict what sequence of actions
	the user is actually doing.  Currently, the user needs to constantly check which
	state the 'add' buttons are in, which shouldn't be necessary.

BF (2001/06/13 10:43:04)
	There are situations when focus is given to an element, where one of the modes
	{add as child, add as sibling} doesn't have any meaning for the element.
	The mode could automatically change for these elements.
	However, for those elements where both modes are meaningful, the mode
	should not change.

title: Import should be smarter (1GE4UZ6) [export/import] [general issue]
description:
Import is very confusing.
	I usually have to import twice to get things put in the right place.  :)
	The import wizard should be smarter (i.e. Java-aware).
	If I select a package in the Packages view and say import, then if I select
	a package tree in the file system that happens to have the exact same name
	as the package I selected... I probably intended to import the classes into
	that package... I probably did *not* intend to create a sub-package with the
	same name...
	For example, if I select org.eclipse.swt, and if I specify to import the following
	directory structure from the file system:
		org
			eclipse
				swt
					<some classes.java>
	then it is silly for the wizard to create:  org.eclipse.swt.org.eclipse.swt
	and import the classes into there. The wizard needs to be much smarter.

	I've observed other users having the same problem.
	We could do a Java specific importer that understands package declarations
	and sets the class path accordingly.

DCR: ability to filter action contributions (menus) by known property
description:
At present, the best way to filter action contributions is via the project 
nature.  However, this solution has undersirable side effects (such as the 
project in-repository being tagged with that nature in its .project, when it 
wasn't intended to share it).

For target management, we would like to have same behaviour as with our use of 
natures to mark a project as belonging to a repo provider, but in this case we 
don't want to use natures for the above reason.

It would be great if we could declare some key in the filtering rules for the 
action, and that key was checked for in project's properties.  This would 
provide considerable flexibility for filtering but avoid having to startup the 
contributing plugin.

title: DCR: PrintDialog should have get/setPrinterData() methods and nothing else (1GFW99N)
description:
Like FontDialog, PrintDialog should have a get/setPrinterData() pair of methods and
	nothing else.  None of what the remainder of PrintDialog's API does anything novel
	or which cannot be done by inspecting or modifying fields of a PrinterData object.
	The functionality that we offer is incomplete as well in that not all features of
	PrinterData can be set/queried in that manner.  Best to stop the duplication now before
	it has the chance to fester and grow.

	At this stage we have few users of PrintDialog, so we may be able to change this without
	much harm.  Otherwise, we can provide the get/setPrinterData() pair, then delegate
	the old methods to use the embedded PrinterData object, and deprecate them.
	I doubt this will raise much of a fuss from our users, if any.

title: [plan item] Allow plug-in deactivation
description:
Allow plug-in deactivation. In order to scale to a large number of plug-ins, 
Eclipse does not activate a plug-in until its code is actually needed. 
However, once activated a plug-in remains active for the remainder of the 
session. Unfortunately, this means that an active plug-in will occupy memory 
space for its code and objects even if it is only used occasionally. Many 
users have sessions lasting days or weeks, and this bloat taxes processor 
memory and JVM performance. The analogy is a long play where the actors enter 
the stage on cue, but cannot leave it until the play is over. The Eclipse 
Platform should support plug-ins that can be safely deactivated when the user 
needs to recover valuable memory space. Another alternative is to provide a 
way to quietly shutdown and restart the Platform. [Platform Core, Platform UI] 
[Theme: Rich client platform]

title: Horizontal scroll bar appears too soon in editor (1GC32LW)
description:
Open a new text file with the default editor.  Start typing text.  The horizontal scroll bar appears before the text has filled 
the width of the page.  This seems odd.  Begin removing text.  The scroll bar does not disappear until all the text has 
been removed from the file.  This seems a bit more odd.

Same thing happens with Java files.

This may be font dependent and may also be an SWT StyledText thing.  


NOTES:

KUM (5/16/01 12:05:40 PM)
	Moved to SWT.

KR (5/23/01 11:36:57 AM)
	The scroll bar appears earlier than necessary because we use a bold font to measure
	the line width. The only way to calculate the line width accurately is by querying the actual 
	line styles and using those to measure the line width. We made a tradeoff of accuracy for speed.

	The scroll bar does not shrink/disappear when you delete text because we only measure
	the lines the change occurred on to check whether they are longer than the current maximum. 
	To get this right we'd have to measure all visible lines when a text change occurs.
	The same is true when scrolling. We only measure the newly visible lines.

	McQ (24/05/2001 11:12:59 AM) -
		This is fine for now. Clearly though, it would be nice if we were more accurate. Have you
		verified that not making the tradeoff for speed makes it too slow?

	McQ (28/05/2001 2:29:16 PM) -
		Not for June.

	McQ (26/06/2001 11:34:43 AM) - 
		We should look at fixing this.

title: [View Mgmt] Part being closed gets partActivation callback for newly active part
description:
build I200211101456

While looking at bug 27646, I saw that the TaskList was being refreshed on 
shutdown.  It was also happening when closing the TaskList.
This is because, when it is closed, it gets a part activation callback for the 
part that will be active after it is closed.
It has no way of knowing that it is in the process of being closed.

We need to ensure that parts get fully closed before a new part is activated.
The order of events should be:
- IWorkbenchPart.dispose()  // for the part being closed
- IPartListener2.partHidden() // for the part being closed
- IPartListener[2].partClosed()   // for the part being closed
- IPartListener2.partVisible() //  for the newly active part
- IPartListener[2].partActivated() // for the newly active part

Should also figure out where partBroughtToTop goes (it's a strange beast).

[Aside: Is there a difference between partVisible and partActivated?  Can you 
show a view without activating it?  I know people have requested this in the 
past, so it doesn't hurt to distinguish between these in case it changes in 
the future.]

We should have tests for this.
It would also be good to specify the order in the Javadoc.

title: [Themes] [JFace] FontRegistry doc needs more detail on font dispose handling by clients
description:
I've noticed that the FontRegistry can dispose of fonts, but it does not 
explain in its documentation when this can happen and what steps a client 
should take to handle these situations.

For example, the put method on FontRegistry will dispose the old font if one 
had been recreated. Before the font is disposed, all listeners are notified of 
the pending font change. We should warn clients of this. It would seem to mean 
that clients that get any fonts from the FontRegistry must add themselves as 
listeners and when a font change is sent to them, get the new font. Or maybe we 
just never dispose of the fonts except when the Display is about to be disposed?

Whatever way we decide to take, we need to document this so the client is not 
left holding onto a disposed font.

title: IServerConnection and buffering of streams
description:
We need to define the buffering relationship between Connection and 
IServerConnection as API and follow this API in our implementations of 
IServerConnection.

Currently, the Connection class wraps the input stream of it's 
IServerConnection in a BufferedInputStream but leaves buffering of the output 
stream up to the IServerConnection. It so happens that PServerConnection also 
buffers the input stream (as well as it's output stream). SSHServerConnection 
also buffers it's input and output streams.

title: Do not provide inappropiate default templates
description:
The 'typecomment' template has the following default value:

/**
 * @version 	1.0
 * @author
 */

The 'filecomment' template has the following default value:

/*
 * (c) Copyright 2001 MyCorporation.
 * All Rights Reserved.
 */

Both of these templates are on by default. This leads to
the Java editor adding inappropriate comments to every source
file generated.

Recommended behavior:
(1) The default 'typecomment' template should be completely empty.
(2) The default 'filecomment' template should be completely empty.
(3) Both templates should be on by default. With empty templates,
bogus class javadoc and file header comments will be not generated.

This means that a user that actually changes these templates to
have suitable values will automatically reap the benefits.

title: Workspace default should be per-user?
description:
I noticed this on Unix (Solaris), but I think it applies to Windows as well:

By default, Eclipse creates a workspace under the Eclipse installation 
directory.  Even though this is a time-honoured tradition for DOS and
Windows programs ("multi-user?  what does that mean?"), I think that this
is the wrong default -- a better default would be to create the workspace
in some per-user area.  This is the norm in Unix, and something like

    new File(new File(System.getProperty("user.home")), ".eclipse")

might do the trick.

Even on a WinNT box we have multiple people using Eclipse, and by default
they all end up using the same workspace, which generally isn't what we
want.

I know that the Eclipse command-line allows you to specify the workspace
location, but I still believe that the common case (default) should be
per-user, not global.

(This is also a more useful default when new Eclipse builds are being 
released on a regular basis -- the workspace default should be outside
the Eclipse distribution, not inside it).

title: [UI] NLS test (JP) - Summary (1GH4KLL)
description:
Here is an initial list of faults I found with Japanese strings.  Some of these problems are
not because the strings are Japanese, but because the strings are generally longer than
english strings.

I will indicate a URL to an image that displays each fault (copy/paste it to explorer/netscape)

1) Edit Action Sets - the list box on the right does not grab excess space.
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls01 (Edit Action Sets).jpg

2) Filter Tasks (Task View) - using the generated strings, this dialog requires a screen resolution
of 1280x1024.  Anything lower and it cannot be fully displayed.  The average user will be using a
lower resolution than this.
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls02 (Filter Tasks).jpg

3) Find/Replace - the title has not been externalized.
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls03 (Find-Replace).jpg

4) All wizards - the title of the message banner cannot display Japanese characters.  I
verified that the characters are in the messages.properties file but I assume this is a
limitation of the font used for the banner title.  example:
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls04 (Save As...).jpg

5) Select Perspective - the list box does not grab excess space.
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls05 (Select Perspective).jpg

6) Show View - the list box does not grab excess space.
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls06 (Show View).jpg

** Wizards setting explicit window size **
7) Export Wizard - i. the 'Back' button is not visible, and the 'Next' button is cut off.
ii. the text of the export types in the list is cut off (in this case the 'File System' in the middle
of the list box (there is a lot of white space that could be used)
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls07 (Export).jpg

8) Import Wizard - i. the 'Back' button is not visible, and the 'Next' button is cut off.
ii. the text of the import types in the list is cut off (in this case the 'File System' in the middle
of the list box (there is a lot of white space that could be used)
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls08 (Import).jpg

9) New Resource Wizard - the 'Back' button is not visible, and the 'Next' button is cut off.
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls09 (New Resource).jpg

10) New Project Wizard - the 'Back' button is not visible, and the 'Next' button is cut off.
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls10 (New Project).jpg

The problem with 7-10 is that wizards are setting an exact size.  This should be set as a
minimum size.  The wizard is resized when next is pressed because the wizard auto-
adjusts its size.
On a related note, two difference sizes are used for wizards: 470x550 and 500x500.
(the first for import/export, the latter for new resources/projects)
Just a suggestion but maybe we should be more consistent by providing a standard
wizard size as Static ints in the WizardDialog class.  We could take this one step further
by adding a method setMinimumSize() that simply sets the dimensions as a minimum size.
This would give wizards a consistent look and feel but would only be optional.
***	***

11) Preference Pages (all) - the text in the banners display block characters instead of the
Japanese characters; probably a font limitation.
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls11 (Preference Page).jpg

12) Property Pages (all) - the text in the banners display block characters instead of the
Japanese characters; probably a font limitation.
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls12 (Property Page).jpg

13) Default Text Editor (Pref Page) - the text 'Default Text Editor Settings' does not show
Japanese characters.  I verified that the characters were present in the .properties file and
verified that it was getting the text from the file.  I don't know why the Japanese characters
don't display because it is using the default font.
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\jp-nls13 (Default Text Editor - Pref).jpg

NOTES:

JEL (23/07/2001 4:07:47 PM)
- One more problem found while testing in German:
14) The 'Select All' button of all import/export wizards on the second page cuts off the text.
This also occurs with Japan strings, just noticed when testing in German.
Q:\viper\team\jlebrun\NLS test\de-nls01 (Import).jpg

JEL (25/07/2001 11:40:21 AM)
RE: 14) The problem here is that the button widths are calculated on the average character size
of the font used.  This is sufficient in most cases.  For the rare case where there are many
fat characters, the estimation will not be large enough.  We can add a safety measure that will
expand the individual button if the estimation is too small.

ex: 	buttonData.widthHint = Math.max(buttonWidth, deselectButton.computeSize(SWT.DEFAULT,SWT.DEFAULT, true).x);
This applies to classes: org.eclipse.ui.wizards.datatransfer::WizardFileSystemResourceImportPage,
and WizardExportResourcesPage
The button will be slightly larger than the other buttons, but at least the text will show.

RE: 7i, 8i, 9, 10) The size is being set, we should check to make sure it is not smaller than the calculated size.

ex: Point size = dialog.getShell().getSize();
	dialog.getShell().setSize( Math.max(SIZING_WIZARD_WIDTH, size.x), Math.max(SIZING_WIZARD_HEIGHT, size.y) );
This applies to classes: org.eclipse.ui.internal::NewProjectAction, ImportResourcesAction, and ExportResourcesAction,
and org.eclipse.ui.actions::NewWizardAction,

title: Need to see "team stream" label on catchup/release (1GDW0WQ)
description:
CVS, SWT
	We have several team streams, i.e. we are not just releasing stuff to "head".
	Therefore, when we are catching up to - or particularly when we are releasing
	- we need to be able to see the name of the team stream.
	The reason this is so necessary is that if we happened to make an error setting
	the management stream for a project, we would get no notification that we were
	releasing into the wrong stream.

	Would be nice if the repository name was also included. (We can envision
	a scenario where you could easily accidentally release code into the wrong
	repository...)

NOTES:

title: [EditorMgmt] DeleteActionHandler.runWithEvent() should not call Text.clearSelection()...
description:
DeleteActionHandler.runWithEvent() in TextActionHandler.java currently calls 
Text.clearSelection().

What this means is that if the user chooses Delete from the Edit menu when an 
editor with an active (owns the keyboard focus) Text widget is present, the 
behaviour is that nothing happens.

The expected behaviour is to have the selection be removed/deleted.

The workaround is possibly to write your own handler.

It seems that this problem exists in versions 2.1.1, 2.1.2, and 3.0M7.

On a related note: CutActionHandler.updateEnabledState() should disable the 
action if the Text is non-editable/disabled.

title: Display.getShell seems to be inefficient (1FY2R0W)
description:
We want to terminate a event loop if no more shells for a given display exists. Using Display.getShells seems to
	be inefficient for this purpose  (two for loops and another two for loops in WidgetTable.getShells()). 

	Is there a better way to determine if a display has open shells than check getShells().length != 0.

NOTES:

	SN (7/14/00 10:54:04 AM)
		Of course there is a better way than building a collection of shells simply to ask for it's length
		but I'm sorry to say that there's no SWT API you can use.  We could consider adding the API
		Display.getShellCount () that could do better or you can simply count the shells that you create
		and dispose and exit your event loop when the count is zero.

	DB (7/17/00 10:05:25 AM) 
		JFace currently maintains and open shell count. But in my opinion this sort of code belongs more
		to SWT than to JFace. So adding the method would simplify code in JFace.

	SN (7/17/00 12:08:05 PM)
		Fine, but there is no OS call in any operating system that answers the top level shell count.
		If SWT is to remain a thin layer on the OS, then we shouldn't be adding convenience API.

	DB (7/21/00 11:37:01 AM)
		I think it should be very simple for SWT to maintain an open shell count, since a shell can only
		be created for a given display. The current implementation in JFace is based on convention (whenever
		you create a shell you have to increment that count) and is therefore susceptible for errors. 

	SN (7/21/00 4:53:00 PM)
		We will consider adding the API.

	McQ (2/2/01 3:34:50 PM) -
		No action.

        int[] intarray = {
                         ^
1 warning

NOTES:

Philippe (10/4/99 3:16:38 PM)
	In presence of wide branches in such code, javac is not using gotow bytecodes (like us), thus leading to 
	illegal code generation. Need to see any use for only making it a warning in order to comply with Sun's behavior.

title: Launch configurations wizard - usability
description:
I've just tried the new Launch Configurations wizard.  It looks pretty cool, 
but I have to admit the UI threw me a bit.  Here are a few that I could sort 
out:

1. Its a single page wizard that allows multiple pages on the right hand side.  
Since there can be more pages then there is room for tabs, you get the '< >' 
arrows to move through the tabs.  I don't recall seeing this anywhere else in 
Eclipse.  It feels like an odd mix between a multi page wizard and a 
preferences wizard.  It may simply work better to have it as a multi page 
wizard, the first page being where you choose an existing configuration or 
create a new one, you can "Next" through the pages which are now tab'd, 
and "Finish" launches.

2. A considerable amount of space is devoted to the left hand tree not leaving 
much space for the right had multi page area.  But once I pick a configuration 
(or create a new one) I really don't need to see that right side anymore.  Thus 
we have an area we don't care much about stealing space from the area we do 
care about. Again, the wizard might work better if these were different pages 
in a multi page wizard.

3. There is a "Debug" button where I would expect there to be an "OK" button.  
I think it would be acceptable and perhaps more familiar to people if the 
wizard simply allowed you to create a new configuration, and then in a 
subsequent step (e.g. in the Debug menu) you chose that configuration to run.  
One odd side effect is that you don't seem to be able to edit the configuration 
without running it, since you can't select "OK".  The non-intuitive workaround 
is that you can do "Apply" and "Cancel".

title: "Click-through" license (1GIRHEV)
description:
Need to add an ability to force a user to accept (or reject) a license agreement prior to downloading and installing
	a component or configuration.

NOTES:
	Candidate for 1.0NL.

	A simple approach for handling this could be to define a convention where the license agreement is placed in a well-known
	file (eg. license.txt) or a well-known key in install.properties. If this file/ key is detected, its content is displayed in a dialog 
	with Accept (allow download and install) and Reject (abort operation) buttons. Note, the mechanism needs to support NL 
	translations, and character encoding (using well known key in install properties make this a simpler implementation, although
	given the complexity + size of some license agreements it may not be the most convenient place).

title: Compare on release is slow (1GEHPR1)
description:
Whenever I attempt to release a whole project, it takes a long time to compute the outgoing changes. 
In some cases, I even know I want to override fully what is on the server, and would be happy with a release no compare.

What I mean is that the release operation should trigger a lazy compare action. It would be fine to simply show me the first affected children
(could be a folder) which I can expand if I do care.

Currently, the comparison is performed until all the leaves, and I can still decide to override conflicting changes all at once (which is fine), so
why then forcing me to get the big penalty upfront when comparing.

NOTES:


JohnA (5/29/2001 11:13:25 AM)
	It isn't comparing any contents, it's just comparing the local workspace with the server to see at a 
	resource granularity what has changed.  This has to happen before you can catchup or release anything,
	because otherwise it doesn't know what to release or load.  We never want to allow releasing without
	first checking if the outgoing change conflicts with changes on the server, so this step is necessary.

Kevinm (5/29/01 3:12:04 PM)
	We should (future) see if this can be sped up though.
	Other thought is that the actual tree filling and comparer opening could be taking time,
	so an optimized (just release if no conflicts) action would be faster.

title: JavaBuilder - Missing libraries results in insufficient dependency info (1FWYERT)
description:
While trying to reproduce 1FWSFNS: ITPJCORE:WIN98 - Assertion Failed in javamodel,
I did the following:

- load RemoteJUnitRunner solution from hydrogen
- it builds
- result is one error in junit.servletui/HTMLWriter.java
  due to missing java.lang.Object
- add rt.jar to class path
- it rebuilds only HTMLWriter.java, producing HTMLWriter.class
- no other .java files are compiled

This is because the compiler aborted early when it detected the missing expected library class.
Only HTMLWriter came back as a result (with proper dependencies).
Since the builder doesn't have dependencies for the other units, it can't know to recompile them
when the missing packages are added.

NOTES:

PM (6/22/00 2:50:16 PM)
	The builder should know it has no build state for the other units.

NE (6/22/00 4:32:55 PM)
	It does, but it can't necessarily act on this knowledge.
	It doesn't know whether the change may fix the problem.
	The only alternative is for it to try recompiling every compilation unit with no dependency info
	every time there is a change, which would be expensive and may not actually fix the problem.

title: Refactoring: operation aren't cancelable since the can't be executed in a different thread. (1GEJ61L)
description:
All refactorings aren't cancelable right now since that aren't executed in a 
separate thread. They have to be executed in the UI thread
	since they are updating documents which trigger events to the editor, 
which updates the UI.

	Possible soultion is to used a special progress monitor that reads the 
event loop on every tick. This would make it possible to 
	cancel an operation even if it is executed in the UI thread.


	See: 1GEJ66W: ITPUI:WIN2000 - Need way to cancel an operation that 
doesn't specify fork= true.

NOTES:

DB (31.07.2001 11:34:49)
	We already have changed the implementation so that a refactoring is 
cancelable during its precondition checking phase. It is not
	cancelable when we the actual code change takes place. In my opinion 
this is the right way to go anyway since:

		- the precondintion checking takes the longest amount of time.
		- the actual change shouldn't be cancelable anyway since the 
program can end up in an inconsistent state. Furthermore it is not
		  possible to generate an undo object for an canceled 
refactoring.
		- the user can undo the refactoring by activating undo.

	Opt to close the PR.

	Waiting for comments from EG and AK.

DB (31.07.2001 16:13:08)
	Not fully true. Precondition checking is only cancelable when pressing 
Next on the first page. When pressing Finish the whole
	operation isn't cancelable at all.

	There are different solutions for that problem:
	
	a.) we post every change to a document into the UI thread. This enables 
to run the operation in a different thread and makes it
	     cancelable.
	b.) the document / document provider or the listener fixes the problem. 
But then JFace Text is the only component that deals with
	     multi thread issues.
	c.) Java Core improves IBuffer in a way that it reports more fine 
grained changes. This would enable the document to keep markers
	     for non changed text segements. If we do that, the Refactoring 
Core could use IBuffer from Java Core to do their text changes instead
	     of IDocument.

	I opt to do c.).

title: Compare browser needs to be smarter
description:
Release a class into the repository.
Now, make changes to a copy of the java file using an external editor outside 
of Eclipse. Add a bunch of new methods, and delete several key old methods. 
Import the file again, over top of the 
This is to simulate running an editing tool like awk or sed or some script on 
the java file, and the tool makes some desired changes, and some undesired 
changes.

But everything should be ok, because you released the class, and you can use 
the Changes browser to simply and easily compare and retrieve the methods that 
were deleted from the class, right?  Wrong.

The Changes or Compare browser needs more work. It does not have the nice 
structured view that the Synchronize browser has. So when looking at a file 
with a massive number of changes when all you want to do is find 3 deleted 
methods is really impossible.  I had over 50 of these files to work on.

The next problem is that "Copy from right to left" doesn't work in the 
SYnchronize browser. So even though I could actually see the exact few methods 
in each class that I needed to pull out of the repository, I couldn't actually 
get at them. (The methods were nicely marked with the '-' sign in the black 
release arrow, but selecting one and saying "Copy from right to left" and Save 
does absolutely nothing).

By the way, when this feature is fixed, I should not have to Save every single 
little "Copy from right to left" - I should be able to click on various 
methods, Copy them to the left, and Save them all in one batch save at the end. 
It's all in the same Java file, so clicking on another method should not 
trigger the "Save" dialog.

title: README: thread termination on JDK 1.3 (1GEYVT8)
description:
DW (6/7/01 3:15:10 PM)
	Thread termination is not supported on JDK 1.3.

	The debugger implements thread termination by invoking #stop on a
	thread with an instance of ThreadDeathException. The debugger
	attempts to create an instance of ThreadDeathException on the first
	class load event received from the VM. On 1.3, the ThreadDeathException
	consrtuctro throws a NullPointerException when invoked before a program
	reaches "main" (not sure why).

	Users should beware not to catch NullPointerException or any of its
	supertypes until after a program has reached main, as this causes the
	attempt to create the ThreadDeathException to suspend, from which the
	debugger may not recover.

DW (6/15/01 10:42:28 AM)
	Added to README.

title: TVT Text extension/truncation problem in jar packager
description:
Messages are truncated on the Jar Packager Dialog. The message format in the US 
english contains trailing spaces after text with a \ presumably marking end of 
message.  One problem we foud was that the tranlation tool mangles the messages 
where multiple messages (6) are moved onto a single line.  The translators did 
find the problem and correcte, putting the (6) messages on seperate lines.  
However, the messages on the dialog were truncated and the buttons were 
scrunched up.  The workaround to this problem is time consumeing and very error 
prone.  Asking the translators to put in the exact number of blanks after there 
NL text as the number of trailing blenks in the US english is not a permenant 
solution.   
 
The corresponding strings are located in file: 
eclipse\plugins\org.eclipse.jdt.ui\jdt_jar\org\eclipse\jdt\internal\ui\jarpackag
er\JarPackagerMessages.properties

title: DCR: No auto tab select on first tab created (1GCEDI4)
description:
Could you change CTabFolder and TabFolder to not auto select the first tab
	that is created? By doing so, it will reduce so draw flash in CTabFolder. Eclipse
	UI already determine which tab should be selected anyway.

	PS Sorry for changing our minds again ;-)

NOTES:

SN (4/19/01 10:35:48 AM)
	For now, we will take out the initial selection for CTabFolder but not all platforms
	support this natively.  We would like to keep the initial selection and fix your code
	for the next release to avoid the flash.

	McQ (26/06/2001 1:07:39 PM) -
		Agree with SN. The first tab should be "selected". Question: Can we just avoid
		doing the callback? Note: This would require changes in the application code,
		so it may be too late to fix this.

tedious. This line toggle functionality exists within the Voice Toolkit within 
the VXML editor which is built upon eclipse.

title: New Class button in empty workspace should be more supportive
description:
User feedback:
"Confused how to create my first project"
We should be more supportive in the UI for this special case since it is a 
first time experience with the UI.

Therefore when the workbench is empty we should offer to create a new Java 
project.
Minimal solution is to show an info dialog that explains that user should 
create a project first and offer a button to open the Java project wizard.

The same is true for the new package and new interface buttons.

title: Create getter and setter insert code into read-only file
Changing target platform location triggers rebuild
description:
Build M5

In the PDE's Target Platform preferences page, I've configured an external 
target.  ('Another compatible application...')

Because of Bug 14270, I temporarily reverted back to using 'This application'.

When I went back to the page to change it back, I clicked on the 'Another 
compatible application' radio button.  As soon as I clicked on the radio 
button, the page triggered a rebuild which took >5 minutes!

Options on a preferences page should not affect the workspace until I 
press 'Apply' or 'Ok'.  And it certainly shouldn't take 5 minutes for the UI 
to return after clicking on a radio button!

This one is particularly troublesome, since clicking on the radio button is 
the only way to enable the text field so that one can enter a new value.  But 
as soon as you click on it, it tries to build based on the old value of the 
field -- I haven't even had a chance to enter the new value yet!

title: [ActionSets] Problems using actionSetPartAssociations
description:
Build 20020321

I have created a action set part association that associates the refactoring 
action set with the packages view and the compilation unit editor (like in the 
documentation). 

Create a fresh workspace reveals the following behaviour:

- focus on packages view: action set visible
- focus on non Welcome editor: action set not visible
- focus on task list: action set not visible

Now, create Test project and a CU A

- focus on Compilation unit editor: action set visible
- focus on task list: action set visible <== ??

Close editor with task list having focus:

- focus on task list: action set visible <== ??
- giving focus to packages view and then back to task list: action 
  set not visible

Ensure task list has focus

- open customize menu
- check refactoring action set
- press ok
- open customize menu
- uncheck refactoring action set
- press ok

Now the action set is completely gone and there is no way to get the old 
behaviour back (where the action set is enabled for packages view and 
compilation unit editor). If I enable the action set, it is enabled for all 
views.

I am aware of the note in the documentation but IMO this is simply not the 
desired behaviour.

title: sync package code review (1GFA13Z)
description:
Random code review comments about types in the sync package:

IRepositoryDeltaCollector method should be renamed to not use CVS-like terminology:
	- shouldn't take MergeResource, need an interface to allow plugin of other implementations.

public void locallyAdded(MergeResource cvsFile);		-> outgoingAdd
public void locallyModified(MergeResource cvsFile);	-> outgoingChange
public void locallyRemoved(MergeResource cvsFile);	-> outgoingDelete
public void needsCheckout(MergeResource cvsFile);	-> incomingChange
public void needsMerge(MergeResource cvsFile);		-> conflictingChange
public void serverAdded(MergeResource cvsFile);		-> incomingAdd
public void serverAddedDirectory(MergeResource cvsFolder); -> Remove (don't need folder special case)
public void serverRemoved(MergeResource cvsFile);	-> incomingDelete
public void unknownStatus(String status);						-> Remove this method

MergeResource can delete the following methods:
	- isLeaf
	- getName
	- getPath
	- getExtension

	replace setLabels with getLocalLabel, getCommonLabel, getRemoteLabel
	rename getLatestRevision to getRemoteEdition
	rename getBaseRevision to getCommonEdition
	remove hasBaseRevision and hasLatestRevision (can use get*Label methods that may return null.

MergeResource can now be a local class of Repository, nobody else needs to know about it.

SyncCompareInput
	- isSaveNeeded should always return false
	- shouldn't be displaying low-level warnings in performSync... should just propagate an exception
	out to the run method, which should use getProblemMessage to show the appropriate message.
	- getProblemTitle should be removed, inline it.
	- getDiffRoot should be removed -- it is a duplicate of CompareEditorInput#getCompareResult
	- SyncCompareInput and MergeCompareInput shouldn't subclass getTitle.  MergeCompareInput should
	just call setTitle in its prepareInput.
	- don't need initialSelectionAndExpansion state, should make use of DiffTreeViewer#navigate,
		this means don't need to subclass createContents.
	- collectParentCreations should be revisited.  Not clear that this is something that we should
		be doing for free.

NOTES:
