title: EC: Feature request: Open multiple editors on Search results (1GJOXY7)
description:
........................................
Reference from newsgroup:

Subject: JDT Views get out of synch
From: wegener@cboe.com (David Wegener)
Newsgroups: eclipse.tools
Organization: EclipseCorner
Date: Sep 05 2001 09:54:43
........................................

Perhaps we can have a setting that not only allows the user to open >1 editors on 
Search results, but perhaps they can set the limit of the number of editors to open.

Steps:
My Steps:
1. Create a Java project and package.
2. In Java perspective, add an interface called MyInterface to the package.
3. Create 2 classes, MyClass1and MyClass2, that each implement MyInterface
4. Close all editors.  (not vital, just makes it easier to see the problem).   
5. In Packages view, select MyInterface.  
6. Bring up context menu and do Search->Implementers.  You should get 2 results in the Search view.
7. In the Search view, double-click (to open) the MyClass2 result.  
8. Now double-click on the MyClass1 result.  
COMPLAINT: Notice that MyClass2 editor has been closed and is replaced by the MyClass1 editor
					  Some users like to be able to open >1 editors open on their search results from the 
					  Search view.
Perhaps this isn't as easy as it sounds.

Here's the post from the newsgroup (there are multiple complaints, I will create other PRs for them):

1) From the Packages view, open a class that implements an interface
that is also implemented by other classes. (Package, editor, Outline all
in synch.)
2) Select the interface name and perform a search for implementers.
(Still in synch)
3) Double Click on one of the other classes that implements the
interface.  (Editor opens on new class with interface name hilighted. 
Packages view still has original class selected, Outline still shows
original class outline.)
4) Close the editor for the second class. (Original class becomes active
in the editor, outline and package view match)
5) Double click on the original class in the search results window.
(Interface name is selected in editor, other views still in synch.)
6) Double click on the second class in the search results window again.
(Original class editor is closed. Packages view still has original class
hilighted, Outline view displays message "An outline is not available").
7) Double click on the original class again.  (Second class editor is
closed and replaced by original.  Packages view still hilights original
class, Outline still shows not available message.)
8) Click in editor window to give it focus.  (Outline displays outline
for original class with nothing hilighted.)

Repeating steps 6-8 continues to close active editor window and opening
new window.  I was also able to produce similar results by searching for
a public static final variable name.  In that case the problem of the
outliner being out of sync caused additional problems. I have the "Show
source of selected element only" option turned on.  Because nothing was
selected in the Outliner, when it did receive focus (to scroll the
member list for example) the package statement would be selected by
default.  This would cause the editor to change from displaying the
method containing the search result to displaying only the package
statement.  You can recreate the situation by selecting the show
selected element only and then clicking on the Outline title bar after
step 6 above.


I would expect the behavior to be the same no matter how elements are
selected to be edited.  Double clicking on a class in the Packages view
opens an editor on the class and brings up the Outline (it should also
select the class in the outline so that the editor doesn't change when
the Outline gets focus.)  Double clicking on a class in the search
results window should do the same thing.  It appears to work better if
the class has previously been opened from the Packages view.

Dave W.

NOTES:
	CM (9/25/2001 12:04:49 PM)
		This is a personal favorite of mine. I would suggest that the solution to this problem
		and all similar problems in all of Eclipse is to establish the following paradigm:
			"Single-click opens temporary editor. Double-click opens persistent editor."

		For details, see: 1GDQA1J: ITPUI:ALL - I really hate the double-click

title: Source Lookup API Change (1GDIS1I)
description: DW (5/9/01 3:04:51 PM) The java workspace source locator is using a stack frame's declaring type name to lookup source. We should reveal the "source name" associated with the stack frame (JDI provides an unqualifed source name - for example "A.java", for type "x.y.A"). The current scheme fails if the (top-level) declaring type name is not the same as the compilation unit name. API Change: Non-breaking method addition package: org.eclipse.jdt.debug interface: IJavaStackFrame method addition: #getSourceName() specification: /** * Returns the unqualified name of the source file this stack frame is associated * with, or null if the source name is not known. For example, if the * declaring type associated with this stack frame is "org.eclipse.example.Example", * the associated source name would be "Example.java". * * @return unqualified source file name, or null * @excetpion DebugException if an exception occurrs retrieving the name from the target */ public String getSourceName(); jeem (5/10/01 2:01:58 PM) - Yep. This should be documented as a non-breaking API change. - declaration is missing throws DebugException - "@excetpion" is misspelled - "occurrs" has just one "r" - example.com is top-level domain reserved for examples; so use "com.example.*" rather than "org.eclipse.example.*" DW (5/10/01 3:12:32 PM) Change integrated. The source lookup should ask a stack frame for its (unqualified) source name, and use the package name portion of the declaring type name to determine which package to look in. If there is no source name available (not in debug attributes), revert to declaring type name. Move to JUI. DW (5/11/01 12:24:22 PM) This fix is available in v0_105_001 in our repository. You should take all our plugins with this version: org.eclipse.debug.core org.eclipse.debug.ui org.eclipse.jdt.debug TM (26.07.2001 09:50:11) Still a problem.

NOTES:

DS (6/12/01 12:01:36 PM)
	Here is the offending code ..

	public IEditorPart openEditor(IMarker marker, boolean activate) 
		throws PartInitException 
	{
		// Get the resource.
		IFile file = (IFile)marker.getResource();		<------ according to exception
		..
	}

	Problem 1: I suspect this exception occurs because the result of getResource is an
	IProject, not an IFile.

	The marker target is a class file in an external jar.  There is no underlying resource for the 
	class file, so I would guess that the java team is hanging the marker on the project itself.  
	Thus, getResource returns an IProject rather than an IFile.  

	If the getResource result is not an IFile there is no way for the workbench to 
	determine the editor input.  IMarker does not provide API to support the scenario.

	Solution: check type of getResource result.  If not IFile show error dialog and return.

	Problem 2: The marker shouldn't even exist.  As stated above, IMarker doesn't provide
	API to get the real marker target.  Our own AddBookmarkAction does not support the
	creation of bookmarks on non-IFiles, so the java team must be defining another 
	bookmark action to bookmark class files.  This is an error.  The packages view 
	should not allow bookmarking on class files.

title: [Viewers] CheckboxTreeViewer's setSubtreeChecked() doesn't work well with deferred content
description:
I have a CheckboxTreeViewer, and there are some long running operations over a
network to provide the content, so I use a DeferredTreeContentManager to fetch
the children, and put a "Pending..." node while it's fetching. So far so good.

I wanted to make it so that checking one item checks all the children
automatically so i tried using setSubtreeChecked(), which is exactly what I was
looking for, and it seems to work, but it causes problems:

1) If I haven't fully expanded my tree yet and I do it, it prevents me from
expanding the tree afterwards past what it was already expanded.
2) There's some flickering with the [+] sign appearing for a short time on the
leaf nodes in the tree.

It appears that it's trying to get all the child items in the tree so that it
can set them as checked, but with deferred content it is seeing the pending item
and stopping there, thinking that's the end of it, while in fact it's not. I am
not sure why it's preventing me from expanding though.

This is not a huge problem because this is just a convenience method - I can
provide my own implementation that works with deferred content.

title: convert field to parameter [refactoring]
description:
Some programmers don't know how to program object oriented and
they program "conventional". They use instance variables 
like global variables in the class.
They set those variable at the beginning of a public method and
use that variable in the following private methods 
instead of passing the variable as parameter.
This hides the use of real instance variables,
which holds the real state of the object,
i.e. the state that resists longer than one public or protected method call.
If have to refactor such code (and perhaps many other people, too).

There already exists the refactoring convert local variable to field.
I never needed that. But I need the refactoring:

"convert field to parameter". If a suspect a field to be a "global variable",
I want to point to it and refactor it. The refactoring tool has to 
analyse whether the field is used in several public/protected methods or 
only in one. In the latter case it can refactor it.

best regards 

Thorsten van Ellen

description:
JGS (5/10/01 7:03:19 PM)
	The icons for variables underneath InspectItems in the Inspector
	look squished.  They don't seem to get as much horizontal space
	as in the variables view, and consequently look different.  

JGS (5/16/01 7:22:24 PM)
	In fact, the whole inspector tree looks like things are squeezed 
together
	more than in the variables view tree.

JGS (5/17/01 11:50:37 AM)
	The reduced space in the inspector also results in the 'S' for static 
variables 
	getting chopped off.

JGS (5/18/01 10:47:58 AM)
	The problem is that the icons of children of an InspectItem are 
OverlayIcons,
	which are 22 pixels wide, whereas the icon for an InspectItem is a 
regular
	icon, which is only 16 pixels wide.  Apparently, the Tree decides how 
much
	space to allow for icons for TreeItems based on how much space the 
parent
	item requires (or it could be how much space the *first* TreeItem 
requires).
	Because of this, 22 pixel wide icons were getting squeezed into 16 
pixels.
	There are a number of ways to fix.  We could make InspectItem public 
API,
	so that JDIModelPresentation could handle its icon, thus allowing it to
	become an OverlayIcon.  But for now, this is fixed by simply widening 
the
	InspectItem icon ("expression_obj.gif")  to be 22 pixels wide.  This 
doesn't require any code changes.  After verifying,
	move this PR to Inactive for reconsideration after first release?

title: [misc] Editor context menu vs. control-F Find menu
description:
As a new Eclipse user (coming from Visual Studio) I find it irritating that 
some search functions are only accessible via control-F (e.g., find and 
replace) and others are available by selecting an identifier, right clicking 
to get a context menu, and then hitting "Search ...".

My preference is that control-F would stay like it is and "Search ..."
would have "find" and "replace" menu entries that would bring up the same
dialog as control-F.  I have two reasons: (1) I have been taught by Windows 
tools that you can do almost everything by context menus (right-mouse-click) 
and I'm used to working that way and (2) I used the mouse to select text, I 
don't like having to move my hand from the mouse to the keyboard to hit 
control-F and then back to the mouse again to deal with the find/replace 
dialog.

Visual Studio has a button with a binocular icon for searching text (your 
control-F).  I miss that button in Eclipse.  They also had a button with 
binoculars and a folder which searched all files in the project for a string 
(it brought up a dialog that let you configure what got searched, but the 
default was all source files in a project).  I also miss that button.

In Visual studio I did not use the context menu to search, as I requested 
above, because these buttons were available.  In Eclipse, when I wanted to 
search and didn't see the binoculars or any other applicable search button, I 
brought up a context menu and saw "Search..." and was happy, but until I later 
found ^F, "Search..." rarely did what I wanted.  By the way, I'm not big on 
reading manuals, unless I have to, so my initial experience with Eclipse may 
not be typical.

Finally, while I'm whining, I want to mention a button in Visual Studio that I 
really liked.  You would select a function or procedure name and hit this 
button and it would display all callers in a context menu.  You then selected 
the caller you wanted and it would navigate to the call.  I used this all the 
time.  Does Eclipse have something like this.

Thanks.

Sam Quiring
sbq@Cayuse.com
503-297-2108 x204

title: [content assist] Autocompletion case-sensitive

title: [UI] EC: Can't contribute submenu items (1GI3XO6)
description:
EC post "Menus and submenus" by GB on Aug 2, 2001: I am trying to create a cascading menu under my own menu. MyMenu Menu1->Submenu1 Submenu2 I cannot get this to work. I can, using the same technique as outlined in the help, add the submenu to the Window menu, and it works. Window Menu1->Submenu1 Submenu2 But when I try to add the submenu to my menu, the menu shows up but it is grayed and none of the Submenu items are available. MyMenu Menu1 (grayed) The log reports 1 org.eclipse.core.resources 4 Invalid Menu Extension (Path is invalid): SubMenu1Id Here is the sample I based the code on. This is from the Eclipse documentation. Here is a version that I got to work in my own application. Here is a version that fails in my application. The only difference is that instead of window, I use MyMenu and instead of additions, I use MyMenu1Slot. I tried variations on ids and slots, but nothing changed. NOTES: NE (8/7/01 5:25:18 PM) Reproduced both success case and fail case. Problem is that the call to parent.findMenuUsingPath(mpath) in PlugActionSetBuilder.contributeMenuAction() returns null when mpath has multiple segments. This is because SubMenuManager.findUsingPath calls findUsingPath on the parentMgr, and MenuManager.findUsingPath tests whether the parent menu is an IMenuManager, which it is not in this case. It was wrapped in an ActionSetContributionItem (subclass of SubContributionItem). Should change SubMenuManager.findUsingPath to recurse itself, unwrapping at each stage. NE (08/07/01 6:01:14 PM) Suggested fix: Change SubContributionManager.find() to unwrap (it doesn't currently, but should): public IContributionItem find(String id) { IContributionItem item = parentMgr.find(id); if (item instanceof SubContributionItem) { return ((SubContributionItem)item).getInnerItem(); } else { return item; } } Change SubMenuManager.getWrapper(IMenuManager) to always create wrapper (as spec'ed). Also added @param tag: /** * Returns the menu wrapper for a menu manager. *

* The sub menus within this menu are wrapped within a SubMenuManager to * monitor additions and removals. If the visibility of this menu is modified * the visibility of the sub menus is also modified. *

* * @param menu the menu manager to wrap * @return the menu wrapper */ private IMenuManager getWrapper(IMenuManager menu) { if (mapMenuToWrapper == null) { mapMenuToWrapper = new HashMap(4); } SubMenuManager wrapper = (SubMenuManager) mapMenuToWrapper.get(menu); if (wrapper == null) { wrapper = wrapMenu(menu); mapMenuToWrapper.put(menu, wrapper); } return wrapper; } Change SubMenuManager.findMenuUsingPath to just call getWrapper() rather than getWrapper then putWrapper if null: public IMenuManager findMenuUsingPath(String path) { IContributionItem item = findUsingPath(path); if (item instanceof IMenuManager) { IMenuManager menu = (IMenuManager)item; return getWrapper(menu); } return null; } Change SubMenuManager.findUsingPath to use same algorithm as MenuManager.findUsingPath, but wrapping submenus along the way: public IContributionItem findUsingPath(String path) { String id = path; String rest = null; int separator = path.indexOf('/'); if (separator != -1) { id = path.substring(0, separator); rest = path.substring(separator + 1); } IContributionItem item = find(id); // unwraps item if (rest != null && item instanceof IMenuManager) { IMenuManager menu = (IMenuManager) item; // wrap menu, just like findMenuUsingPath IMenuManager wrapper = getWrapper(menu); return wrapper.findUsingPath(rest); } return item; } Delete SubMenuManager.putWrapper -- it's no longer needed.

	failed, and disable the breakpoint.

title: Need replacement for #hasChildren()
description:
In R1.0 the "hasChildren()" method call was used to determine if a "+" was
to be shown on a tree node in
for example the Variables view.
This worked well because a StackFrame could respond that there were
children without actually
getting them.

In R2.0 this has changed to call the IDebugElement's method that returns
its "elements".
e.g for IStackFrame the getVariables() method is called.

The problem is that the Variable's view caches the response and therefore
requires that our
debug element return a full and correct list.   In some cases this can
cause the debug engine to do lots of
processing for something that the user may never expand.

This can be very costly.

What it needs in addition to IStackFrame.getVariables() is a method called
"boolean IStackFrame.hasVariables()"
that would allow engines to respond that there are variables without
actually having to get them.

title: [templates] Nested Templates
description:
Brace yourselves...

I would like to be able to nest templates by specifying that a template A 
should be embedded in the ${cursor} position of template B.

For example, a method to print out the contents of an array could be defined 
thus:

template(public_method, template(for, stdout))

when invoked, working from the inside out, the stdout template is used - there 
is only one.
Then, the user would be prompted for which 'for' template to use (there are 3), 
and insert the stdout template into the ${cursor} position of the chosen 'for' 
template. 
Then, the 'for' template would be inserted into the ${cursor} position of the 
public_method template.

The cursor would be placed in the ${cursor} position of the stdout template 
since this is the only place with a cursor position left.

The only thing to be careful of is cycles.

title: [Contributions] updating: Need hooks to control enablement of global menu items
description:
Currently, all refactoring actions are enabled when the Java editor has focus. 
This is the case, since the Java editor doesn't sent out selection changes for 
all cursor changes (doing so would highly impact typing). Those are only 
reported by post selection changes.

We have several requests that only those refactoring actions should be enabled 
which are applicable to the current selection. I add support for this to the 
context menu by computing the enablement state when the pop-up menu becomes 
visible. I would like to add the same support to the global refactoring menu. 
To do so I need a hook when:

- the user presses a short cut
- the refactoring menu opens
- the refactoring menu closes

Can those hooks be provided ?

title: [Sync View] Usability: meaningless message "operation in progress..."
description:
After installing a brand new copy of eclipse v3.0, I attempt to share a project
that was previously shared using eclipse v3.0M9.

I make sure "validate the connection" is not checked.

I choose the project and select "synchronise with repository". At this point, a
popup window appears saying "Operation in progress..." and the "details" button
is greyed out.

At this point the "operation in progress..." message is entirely meaningless. An
operation is obviously in progress, the hourglass mouse cursor tells me so. The
message does not tell me _which_ operation is in progress, so I am left with no
information describing what eclipse is trying to do, and therefore no means to
debug the underlying problem without lots of groping around in the dark.

The fix: remove this message entirely, or replace it with a meaningful
indication of what eclipse is doing.

Pressing "cancel" on the message dialog has the effect of greying out the cancel
button. The "operation in progress" is not cancelled. Attempts at clicking on
"close window" are ignored. Eclipse has now hung and needs to be killed.

This bug is probably related to bug 69946.

The task at hand is a CVS operation - in the past, I would have been presented
with a dialog box asking me for my login password to the CVS repository. I
strongly suspect the underlying problem is caused by the CVS section waiting for
a password from a dialog box that is never shown on the screen. v3.0M9 shows an
IOException explaining that a timeout has occurred. v3.0 final does not time out
at all, and has to be killed, losing all unsaved changes.

title: Project Sets: Cannot easily find file I saved
description:
(Note that I'm on Win98 other OS may differ)
I performed a project export, choose all my projects and chose Browse to 
specify a file to save to. The dialog had a drop down list of types which 
contained one entry (Team Project Set Files). Since I have no clue what the 
proper extension is, I entered a name with no extension, expecting that the 
proper extension would be appended.

On import, I browse to the directory where I saved my file and I can't see it. 
I had to enter *.* in the text field to see the file. It was saved with no 
extension.

I think the following should be done.
1. If the user doesn't provide an extension, the proper one should be added 
(many programs do this).

title: Export wizard should expand to preselections (1GIGC8W)
error in Preferences dialog not displayed after hitting Tab (1GCGEY2)
description:
If an error is displayed in the Preferences dialog, then you hit Tab to change the 
focus to a button, the error is no longer displayed, even though the problem is 
still there.

*Window->Preferences
*Select Java->Runtimes->JDK1.2
*Click Browse
*Select some random invalid (i.e. does not contain a JDK) directory
*Hit OK.
*Notice the error in the banner area of the Preferences dialog
*Hit Tab (once or twice) until the Defaults button has focus 
*The error in the banner area of the dialog is not longer displayed

NOTES:
	RG (5/11/01 4:38:40 PM) 
	This is because 
	org.eclipse.jface.preference.StringFieldEditor.getTextControl(Composite)
	sets a focus lost listener on its conctrol and calls clearError message when
	the text contol loses focus.
	Interestingly it does not validate until focus is lost so one gets no error
	message even if there is one. Just after validate displays a message,
	the message is cleared.

your workbench window was maximized at the time, you can't access the
windows behind the workbench.  Need to be able to manipulate windows
while an operation is in progress.
